title.zh: 卷八十三 列傳第四十三 宗越 吳喜 黃回
title.en: Volume 83 Biographies 43: Zong Yue, Wu Xi, Huang Hui
title.raw: 卷八十三 列傳第四十三 宗越 吳喜 黃回 Volume 83 Biographies 43: Zong Yue, Wu Xi, Huang Hui

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十三 宗越 吳喜 黃回

translations.literal: Biographies 43: Zong Yue, Wu Xi, Huang Hui
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 43: Zong Yue, Wu Xi, and Huang Hui

sentences.zh: 宗越，南陽葉人也。

translations.literal: Zong Yue was a man of Ye in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yue was a native of Ye in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 本河南人，晉亂，徙南陽宛縣，又土斷屬葉。

translations.literal: Originally he was a man of Henan; in the Jin turmoil [his clan] moved to Wan County in Nanyang, and through territorial registration was assigned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: His family was originally from Henan; during the turmoil of the Jin they moved to Wan County in Nanyang, and through territorial registration were reassigned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 本為南陽次門，安北將軍趙倫之鎮襄陽，襄陽多雜姓，倫之使長史范覬之條次氏族，辨其高卑，覬之點越為役門。

translations.literal: Originally of secondary-gate status in Nanyang, when General Who Pacifies the North Zhao Lunzhi was stationed at Xiangyang—Xiangyang had many mixed surnames—Lunzhi had his Chief of Staff Fan Xianzhi arrange the clans in order and distinguish high from low; Xianzhi classified Yue as service-gate status.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had held secondary-gate standing in Nanyang. When General Who Pacifies the North Zhao Lunzhi governed Xiangyang, where many mixed surnames lived, Lunzhi had his chief of staff Fan Xianzhi rank the clans and sort high from low; Xianzhi placed Yue in the service gate.

sentences.zh: 出身補郡吏。

translations.literal: He entered service and was appointed a commandery clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a commandery clerk.

sentences.zh: 父為蠻所殺，殺其父者嘗出郡，越於市中刺殺之，太守夏侯穆嘉其意，擢為隊主。

translations.literal: His father was killed by barbarians; the man who had killed his father once left the commandery, and Yue stabbed him to death in the market. The Administrator Xia Houmu admired his purpose and promoted him to platoon chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father was killed by barbarians. When the killer once left the commandery, Yue stabbed him in the marketplace. Prefect Xia Houmu admired his resolve and promoted him to platoon chief.

sentences.zh: 蠻有為寇盜者，常使越討伐，往輒有功。

translations.literal: When barbarians became bandits, they often sent Yue to suppress them; whenever he went he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever barbarians raided, the authorities sent Yue against them, and he always won.

sentences.zh: 家貧無以市馬，常刀楯步出，單身挺戰，眾莫能當。

translations.literal: His family was poor and had no means to buy a horse; he regularly went out on foot with blade and shield, fighting alone in the van, and none could withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to buy a horse, he often marched out on foot with sword and shield, charging alone into battle, and no one could stand against him.

sentences.zh: 每一捷，郡將輒賞錢五千，因此得市馬。

translations.literal: After each victory the commandery general would reward him with five thousand cash, and thus he was able to buy a horse.
translations.idiomatic: After every victory the commandery commander gave him five thousand cash, and in this way he finally bought a horse.

sentences.zh: 後被召，出州為隊主。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and left the province to serve as platoon chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned from the province to serve as platoon chief.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮襄陽，以為揚武將軍，領臺隊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was stationed at Xiangyang, [Yue] was made General Who Raises Martiality and placed in charge of the capital guard detachment.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xiaowu held Xiangyang, Yue was appointed General Who Raises Martiality and put in command of the capital guard company.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年，啟太祖求復次門，移戶屬冠軍縣，許之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia he petitioned the Founder to restore secondary-gate status and move his household register to Guanjun County; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia he petitioned Emperor Wu to restore his clan's secondary-gate standing and transfer his household to Guanjun County; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，隨柳元景北伐，領馬幢，隸柳元怙，有戰功，事在元景傳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he followed Liu Yuanjing on the northern campaign, commanded the horse pennant, served under Liu Yuanhu, and had battle merit—the account is in Yuanjing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he joined Liu Yuanjing's northern campaign, led the horse pennant, and served under Liu Yuanhu with distinction; the details appear in Yuanjing's biography.

sentences.zh: 還補後軍參軍督護，隨王誕戲之曰：「汝何人，遂得我府四字。」

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Rear Army Staff Officer and Protector. Prince Dan of Sui joked with him, saying, "Who are you, that you should get the four characters of my command's [title]?"
translations.idiomatic: After he returned he was made rear-army staff officer and protector. Prince Dan of Sui teased him, saying, "Who are you to carry the four characters of my command staff on your title?"

sentences.zh: 越答曰：「佛狸未死，不憂不得諮議參軍。」

translations.literal: Yue replied, "As long as Buddha Li is not dead, do not worry about not becoming Advisory Army Staff Officer."
translations.idiomatic: Yue answered, "While Buddha Li still lives, you need not worry about my not becoming an advisory army staff officer."

sentences.zh: 誕大笑。

translations.literal: Dan laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: Dan burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵反，越領馬軍隸沈慶之攻誕。

translations.literal: When Prince Dan of Jingling seized Guangling in rebellion, Yue led the cavalry under Shen Qingzhi to attack Dan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled and held Guangling, Yue led the cavalry under Shen Qingzhi to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，世祖使悉殺城內男丁，越受旨行誅，躬臨其事，莫不先加捶撻，或有鞭其面者，欣欣然若有所得，所殺凡數千人。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Emperor Xiaowu ordered all males in the city killed. Yue received the decree to carry out executions and personally oversaw the matter; none were not first beaten with cudgels, and some had their faces whipped. He was delighted as if gaining something; those killed totaled several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, Emperor Xiaowu ordered every male inside killed. Yue took the order to execute them and oversaw the work himself. He had each man beaten first; some were flogged across the face. He looked pleased, as though he had gained something. Several thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 四年，改封始安縣子，戶邑如先。

translations.literal: In the fourth year [of Daming] he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shi'an, with fief households as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shi'an, with the same fief households as before.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷新安王子鸞撫軍中兵參軍，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Army Staff Officer under the Heir Apparent of Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, and given the additional title General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became army staff officer to Prince Ziluan of Xin'an's heir apparent, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 其年，督司州、豫州之汝南、新蔡、汝陽、潁川四郡諸軍事、寧朔將軍、司州刺史，尋領汝南、新蔡二郡太守。

translations.literal: That year he was made Commander of military affairs for the four commanderies of Runan, Xincai, Ruyang, and Yingchuan in Sizhou and Yuzhou, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Sizhou; soon thereafter he also held the governorships of Runan and Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was appointed to command military affairs in Runan, Xincai, Ruyang, and Yingchuan—the four commanderies of Sizhou and Yuzhou—as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Sizhou, and soon afterward also governed Runan and Xincai.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年，召為游擊將軍，直閣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe of the Deposed Former Emperor, he was summoned as General Who Strikes the Enemy and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe under the Deposed Former Emperor, he was recalled as General Who Strikes the Enemy and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 頃之，領南濟陰太守，進爵為侯，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he took charge of Nan Jiyin as Administrator, was advanced to Marquis, with an increase of two hundred fief households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he took over Nan Jiyin as administrator, was promoted to marquis, and gained two hundred fief households.

sentences.zh: 又加冠軍將軍，改領南東海太守，游擊如故。

translations.literal: He was further given the title General Who Champions the State and transferred to Governor of Nan Donghai, his post as Striking General unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made General Who Champions the State and reassigned to govern Nan Donghai while keeping his striking-general post.

sentences.zh: 帝兇暴無道，而越及譚金、童太壹並為之用命，誅戮群公及何邁等，莫不盡心竭力。

translations.literal: The Emperor was ferocious and without principle, yet Yue along with Tan Jin and Tong Taiyi all obeyed his orders and carried out the slaughter of the leading officials including He Mai and the rest, each exerting utmost loyalty and strength.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was brutal and lawless, yet Yue, Tan Jin, and Tong Taiyi all obeyed him without question, slaughtering the great ministers and men such as He Mai with tireless zeal.

sentences.zh: 故帝憑其爪牙，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: Therefore the Emperor relied on them as his claws and fangs and feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thus leaned on them as his claws and fangs and feared no one.

sentences.zh: 賜與越等美女金帛，充牣其家。

translations.literal: He bestowed on Yue and the others beautiful women, gold, and silk, filling their houses to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished on Yue and the others beautiful women, gold, and silk until their houses overflowed.

sentences.zh: 越等武人麤彊，識不及遠，咸一往意氣，皆無復二心。

translations.literal: Yue and the others were coarse, strong fighting men whose vision did not reach far; they all threw themselves into service with single intent and never again had second thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: These men were rough soldiers of limited foresight; they threw themselves into the work with one-minded loyalty and never wavered.

sentences.zh: 帝將欲南巡，明旦便發，其夕悉聽越等出外宿，太宗因此定亂。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to tour south and would set out the next morning, that evening he allowed Yue and the others to lodge outside; Emperor Ming thus secured the coup.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a southern tour and would depart the next morning, that evening he let Yue and the others sleep outside the palace—giving Emperor Ming his chance to seize power.

sentences.zh: 明晨，越等竝入，上撫接甚厚，越改領南濟陰太守，本官如故。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Yue and the others all entered [court]; the Emperor received them with great warmth. Yue was reassigned as Administrator of Nan Jiyin, his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yue and the others all came in; the new emperor received them warmly. Yue was reassigned to govern Nan Jiyin while keeping his former posts.

sentences.zh: 越等既為廢帝盡力，慮太宗不能容之，上接待雖厚，內竝懷懼。

translations.literal: Yue and the others, having exhausted themselves for the deposed emperor, feared that Emperor Ming could not tolerate them. Although the Emperor received them with apparent kindness, inwardly they were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Having given everything to the deposed emperor, Yue and his fellows feared Emperor Ming would not spare them. Though the court treated them generously, inwardly they were terrified.

sentences.zh: 上亦不欲使其居中，從容謂之曰：「卿等遭罹暴朝，勤勞日久，苦樂宜更，應得自養之地。

translations.literal: The Emperor also did not wish to keep them at court center and said calmly, "You endured a brutal reign and toiled long; bitter and sweet should change—there ought to be a place where you can restore yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also did not want them at the capital and said gently, "You suffered under a violent reign and labored long. It is time your fortunes changed—you deserve a place to rest and recover.

sentences.zh: 兵馬大郡，隨卿等所擇。」

translations.literal: Choose whichever large commandery with troops you wish."
translations.idiomatic: Pick any great commandery with troops that suits you."

sentences.zh: 越等素已自疑，及聞此旨，皆相顧失色，因謀作難。

translations.literal: Yue and the others had already been suspicious, and when they heard these words they looked at one another in dismay and thus plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Already uneasy, Yue and the others turned pale at these words and plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 以告沈攸之，攸之具白太宗，即日收越等下獄死。

translations.literal: They told Shen Youzhi; Youzhi reported fully to Emperor Ming, and that same day Yue and the others were arrested, imprisoned, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: They confided in Shen Youzhi, who reported everything to Emperor Ming. That same day Yue and his companions were arrested and executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 越時年五十八。

translations.literal: Yue was then fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was fifty-eight at the time.

sentences.zh: 越善立營陣，每數萬人止頓，越自騎馬前行，使軍人隨其後，馬止營合，未嘗參差。

translations.literal: Yue excelled at establishing camps. Whenever tens of thousands halted, Yue rode ahead on horseback and had the soldiers follow behind; when his horse stopped the camp was formed—never once out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was skilled at pitching camps. When tens of thousands halted, he rode ahead on horseback while the troops followed; when his horse stopped, the encampment was complete—never a step out of line.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之代殷孝祖為南討前鋒，時孝祖新死，眾並懼，攸之歎曰：「宗公可惜，故有勝人處。」

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi replaced Yin Xiaozu as vanguard of the southern campaign, Xiaozu had just died and the troops were all afraid. Youzhi sighed and said, "Lord Zong was a pity—he had what it took to excel over others."
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi replaced Yin Xiaozu as southern campaign vanguard, Xiaozu had just died and the army was shaken with fear. Youzhi sighed, "A pity about Lord Zong—he truly had his strengths."

sentences.zh: 而御眾嚴酷，好行刑誅，睚眥之間，動用軍法。

translations.literal: Yet in commanding troops he was harsh and fond of punishments; over the smallest grudge he would apply military law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in command he was harsh and fond of executions; the slightest grudge could bring military punishment.

sentences.zh: 時王玄謨御下亦少恩，將士為之語曰：「寧作五年徒，不逐王玄謨。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Xuomo too was sparing of kindness to subordinates, and the officers and men said of it, "Better five years as a convict than serve under Wang Xuomo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuomo was likewise stingy with mercy toward his men, and soldiers said, "Better five years as a convict than follow Wang Xuomo.

sentences.zh: 玄謨尚可，宗越殺我。」

translations.literal: Xuomo is still endurable; Zong Yue will kill you."
translations.idiomatic: Xuomo is still tolerable; Zong Yue will kill you."

sentences.zh: 譚金，荒中傖人也。

translations.literal: Tan Jin was a man of the wilderness, a Shang from the wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Jin was a Shang tribesman from the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 在荒中時，與薛安都有舊，後出新野，居牛門村。

translations.literal: While in the wilderness he had been old friends with Xue Anu; later he came out to Xinye and lived at Niumen Village.
translations.idiomatic: In the wild country he had been close to Xue Anu; later he came out to Xinye and settled at Niumen Village.

sentences.zh: 及安都歸國，金常隨征討。

translations.literal: When Anu returned to the state, Jin regularly followed him on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: When Anu submitted to the dynasty, Jin followed him on campaign after campaign.

sentences.zh: 自北入崤陝，及巴口建義，恆副安都，排堅陷陣，氣力兼人，平元兇及梁山破臧質，每有戰功。

translations.literal: From the north he entered through the Xia and Shan passes, and at the Ba crossing during the founding uprising he constantly served Anu as deputy, breaking hardened positions—his strength matched several men. In pacifying the prime rebel and at Liangshan breaking Zang Zhi he won merit each time.
translations.idiomatic: He entered from the north through the Xia and Shan passes; at the Ba crossing, when the founding uprising began, he constantly served at Anu's side, smashing strong lines with strength equal to several men. He won merit in crushing the chief rebel and in the defeat of Zang Zhi at Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 稍至建平王宏中軍參軍事，加建武將軍，尋轉龍驤將軍、南下邳太守，參軍如故。

translations.literal: He gradually rose to Acting Army Staff Officer under Prince Hong of Pingling, with the additional title General Who Establishes Martiality; soon he became General Who Inspires Awe and Administrator of Nan Xiapi, retaining his staff post.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to acting army staff officer under Prince Hong of Pingling, with the additional rank of General Who Establishes Martiality, then became General Who Inspires Awe and administrator of Nan Xiapi while keeping his staff duties.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，遷屯騎校尉、直閣，領南清河太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian he was moved to Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry and Palace Attendant, holding governorship of Nan Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian he was promoted to colonel of the valiant cavalry and palace attendant, governing Nan Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，前廢帝誅群公，金等並為之用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe the Deposed Former Emperor slaughtered the leading officials, and Jin and the others served him in it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe, when the Deposed Former Emperor killed the great ministers, Jin and his fellows carried out his orders.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔曰：「屯騎校尉南清河太守譚金、彊弩將軍童太壹、車騎中兵參軍沈攸之，誠略沈果，忠幹勇鷙，消蕩氛翳，首制鯨凶，宜裂河山，以酬勳義。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict saying, "Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry and Administrator of Nan Qinghe Tan Jin, General of the Strong Crossbows Tong Taiyi, and Army Staff Officer of the Heir Apparent of the Chariots and Cavalry Shen Youzhi are deep in stratagem and resolute in action, loyal, capable, and fiercely brave. They have cleared away the miasma of treason and were first to seize the great villain. Rivers and mountains should be divided to reward their merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict: "Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry and Administrator of Nan Qinghe Tan Jin, General of the Strong Crossbows Tong Taiyi, and army staff officer to the heir apparent of the chariots and cavalry Shen Youzhi are resolute in counsel and deed, loyal, able, and fiercely brave. They have swept away the fog of rebellion and were first to bring down the great traitor. Their achievements deserve a share of the realm itself.

sentences.zh: 金可封平都縣男，太壹宜陽縣男，攸之東興縣男，食邑各三百戶。」

translations.literal: Jin may be enfeoffed as Baron of Pingdu, Taiyi as Baron of Yiyang, and Youzhi as Baron of Dongxing, each with a fief of three hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: Jin shall be enfeoffed as Baron of Pingdu, Taiyi as Baron of Yiyang, and Youzhi as Baron of Dongxing, each with three hundred fief households."

sentences.zh: 金遷驍騎將軍，增邑百戶。

translations.literal: Jin was moved to General of the Valiant Cavalry, with an increase of one hundred fief households.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was promoted to general of the valiant cavalry and given one hundred additional fief households.

sentences.zh: 太壹，東莞人也。

translations.literal: Taiyi was a man of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyi was a native of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 自彊弩遷左軍將軍，增邑百戶。

translations.literal: From General of the Strong Crossbows he was moved to General of the Left Army, with an increase of one hundred fief households.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred from general of the strong crossbows to general of the left army and gained one hundred more fief households.

sentences.zh: 金、太壹竝與宗越俱死。

translations.literal: Jin and Taiyi both died together with Zong Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Taiyi were executed together with Zong Yue.

sentences.zh: 越州里劉胡、武念、佼長生、蔡那、曹欣之，竝以將帥顯。

translations.literal: In Yue's home commandery, Liu Hu, Wu Nian, Jiao Changsheng, Cai Na, and Cao Xinzhi all became famous as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: From Yue's home region, Liu Hu, Wu Nian, Jiao Changsheng, Cai Na, and Cao Xinzhi all rose to prominence as generals.

sentences.zh: 劉胡事在鄧琬傳。

translations.literal: Liu Hu's account is in the biography of Deng Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu's story is told in the biography of Deng Wan.

sentences.zh: 武念，新野人也。

translations.literal: Wu Nian was a man of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Nian was a native of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 本三五門，出身郡將。

translations.literal: Originally of the Three-Five Gate, he entered service as a commandery commander.
translations.idiomatic: His clan belonged to the Three-Five Gate; he began as a commandery officer.

sentences.zh: 蕭思話為雍州，遣土人龐道符統六門田，念為道符隨身隊主。

translations.literal: When Xiao Sihua was Governor of Yongzhou, he sent the local man Pang Daofu to oversee the six-gate fields; Nian served as Daofu's personal platoon chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Sihua governed Yongzhou, he put the local leader Pang Daofu in charge of the six-gate estates, and Nian became Daofu's personal platoon chief.

sentences.zh: 後大府以念有健名，且家富有馬，召出為將。

translations.literal: Later the great commandery office, because Nian had a reputation for strength and his family was wealthy in horses, summoned him out to serve as a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later the regional headquarters, noting his reputation for prowess and his family's horses, called him up as a field commander.

sentences.zh: 世祖臨雍州，念領隊奉迎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took Yongzhou, Nian led a company to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu assumed Yongzhou, Nian led troops to receive him.

sentences.zh: 時沔中蠻反，世祖之鎮，緣道討伐，部伍至大堤岩洲，蠻數千人忽至，乘高矢射雨下。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarians of the Han River rebelled; during Emperor Xiaowu's tenure he campaigned along the route. When his unit reached the Dayanzhou of Dadi, several thousand barbarians suddenly appeared, shooting arrows like rain from the heights.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians along the Han had risen in revolt. While Emperor Xiaowu held the province he marched against them along the route. Near Dadi's Dayanzhou, several thousand barbarians suddenly appeared on the heights and rained arrows down.

sentences.zh: 念馳赴奮擊，應時摧退，即擢為參軍督護。

translations.literal: Nian galloped forward and struck fiercely, repelling them at once, and was immediately promoted to Army Staff Officer and Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Nian charged forward and fought fiercely, driving them off at once, and was immediately promoted to army staff officer and protector.

sentences.zh: 其後每軍旅，常有戰功。

translations.literal: Afterward, in every campaign he regularly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: After that he distinguished himself in campaign after campaign.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建中，為建威將軍、桂陽太守。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian era of Emperor Xiaowu he was made General Who Establishes Martiality and Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaowu's Xiaojian reign he became General Who Establishes Martiality and administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕反，念以江夏王義恭太宰參軍、龍驤將軍，隸沈慶之攻廣陵城。

translations.literal: When Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled, Nian served as army staff officer to the Grand Tutor of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and as General Who Inspires Awe, under Shen Qingzhi in the attack on Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled, Nian served as army staff officer to Prince Yigong of Jiangxia in his role as grand tutor and as General Who Inspires Awe under Shen Qingzhi at the siege of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 誕出城走，既而復還，念追之不及，坐免官。

translations.literal: Dan fled the city but then returned; Nian pursued but could not overtake him and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Dan fled the city, then turned back; Nian pursued but failed to catch him and was removed from his post.

sentences.zh: 復以為冗從僕射，出為龍驤將軍、南陽太守。

translations.literal: He was again made Supernumerary Attendant of the Heir Apparent and sent out as General Who Inspires Awe and Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made supernumerary attendant of the heir apparent and sent out as General Who Inspires Awe and administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和中，為右軍將軍，直閣，封開國縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era of the Deposed Former Emperor he was made General of the Right Army and palace attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Kaiguo with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Former Emperor in the Jinghe era he became general of the right army and palace attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Kaiguo with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，四方反叛，遣念乘驛還雍州，綏慰西土，因以為南陽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first took the throne, rebellion broke out on all sides; he sent Nian by post horse back to Yongzhou to pacify the western lands and appointed him Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming first ascended the throne, rebellions flared everywhere. He sent Nian by relay horse to Yongzhou to reassure the west and made him administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 念既至，人情並向之，劉胡遣腹心數騎詐詣念降，於坐縛念，袁顗斬之，送首詣晉安王子勛。

translations.literal: After Nian arrived, popular sentiment all turned toward him. Liu Hu sent several trusted horsemen pretending to surrender to Nian and, at the meeting, bound him. Yuan Yi executed him and sent his head to Prince Zixun of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Once Nian arrived, the people rallied to him. Liu Hu sent a few trusted riders feigning surrender; at the meeting they seized Nian. Yuan Yi beheaded him and sent the head to Prince Zixun of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 念黨袁處珍逃亡至壽陽，為逆黨劉順所得，考楚備至，秉義不移，後得叛奔劉勔；

translations.literal: Nian's follower Yuan Chuzhen fled to Shouyang, was seized by the rebel Liu Shun, and was tortured to the utmost yet held to righteousness without wavering; later he escaped the rebels and fled to Liu Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Nian's follower Yuan Chuzhen fled to Shouyang, was captured by the rebel Liu Shun, and was tortured without end yet would not yield; later he broke away and joined Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，以為奉朝請。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming praised this and made him a Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming commended his loyalty and appointed him court gentleman for the imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 追贈念冠軍將軍、南陽、新野二郡太守，封綏安縣侯，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Posthumously Nian was given the title General Who Champions the State and the governorships of Nanyang and Xinye, enfeoffed as Marquis of Suian with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Nian was posthumously made General Who Champions the State and governor of Nanyang and Xinye, enfeoffed as Marquis of Suian with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，綏安縣省，改封邵陵縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, Suian County was abolished and [the title] was changed to Marquis of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi, Suian County was abolished and the marquisate was transferred to Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 佼長生，廣平人也。

translations.literal: Jiao Changsheng was a man of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Changsheng was a native of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 出身為縣將，大府以其有膂力，召為府將。

translations.literal: He entered service as a county commander; the great commandery office, because he had physical strength, summoned him as a commandery guard.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a county commander; the regional headquarters, impressed by his strength, called him up as a commandery guard.

sentences.zh: 朱脩之拒魯秀于峴南，長生有戰功，稍見任使。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xiuzhi resisted Lu Xiu south of Xian, Changsheng had battle merit and gradually came to be employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xiuzhi held Lu Xiu south of Xian, Changsheng won distinction and gradually won trust.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，為建安王休仁司徒中兵參軍，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he was made Army Staff Officer to the Heir Apparent of Prince Xiuren of Jian'an, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign he became army staff officer to Prince Xiuren of Jian'an's heir apparent, with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 南討有功，封遷陵縣侯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: He had merit in the southern campaign and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianling with a fief of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the southern campaigns and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qianling with eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後為張悅寧遠司馬，寧蠻校尉。

translations.literal: Later he was made Chief of Staff to Zhang Yue, Pacifier of the Far, and Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Zhang Yue as chief of staff for the Pacification of the Far and as colonel who pacifies the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，卒，追贈征虜將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi he died; posthumously he was given the title General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Taishi and was posthumously made General Who Conquers the Barbarians and governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 曹欣之，新野人也。

translations.literal: Cao Xinzhi was a man of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xinzhi was a native of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 積勤勞，後廢帝元徽初，為軍主。

translations.literal: Through accumulated labor, at the beginning of Yuanhui of the Later Deposed Emperor he was made an army commander.
translations.idiomatic: After long service, at the start of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor he became an army commander.

sentences.zh: 以平桂陽王休範功，封新市縣子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Prince Xiufan of Guiyang he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinshi with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing Prince Xiufan of Guiyang he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinshi with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 為左軍驍騎將軍，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was made General of the Valiant Cavalry of the Left Army, with the additional title General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He became general of the valiant cavalry of the left army, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年，以本號為徐州刺史、鍾離太守，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui, with his existing title he was made Governor of Xuzhou and Administrator of Zhongli, advanced to General Who Champions the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhui he was made governor of Xuzhou and administrator of Zhongli under his existing title, and promoted to General Who Champions the State.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明二年，徵為散騎常侍、驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming of Emperor Shun he was summoned as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun he was recalled as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and general of the valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year.

sentences.zh: 吳喜，吳興臨安人也。

translations.literal: Wu Xi was a man of Lin'an in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi was a native of Lin'an in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 本名喜公，太宗減為喜。

translations.literal: His original name was Xigong; Emperor Ming shortened it to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Xigong; Emperor Ming shortened it to Xi.

sentences.zh: 初出身為領軍府白衣吏。

translations.literal: He first entered service as a white-robed clerk in the Heir Apparent's command.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a junior clerk in the heir apparent's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 少知書，領軍將軍沈演之使寫起居注，所寫既畢，闇誦略皆上口。

translations.literal: In youth he knew books; General of the Heir Apparent's Army Shen Yanzhi had him copy the imperial diary. When the copying was finished, he could recite it from memory with few omissions.
translations.idiomatic: He learned to read early. General of the heir apparent's army Shen Yanzhi had him copy the imperial diary; when the work was done he could recite nearly all of it from memory.

sentences.zh: 演之嘗作讓表，未奏，失本，喜經一見，即便寫赴，無所漏脫，演之甚知之。

translations.literal: Yanzhi once drafted a memorial of resignation that had not yet been submitted when the original was lost; after one reading Xi copied it out and sent it in without omission, and Yanzhi thought highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi once wrote a resignation memorial that had not been submitted when the draft was lost. Xi saw it once, reproduced it completely, and Yanzhi was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 因此涉獵《史》、《漢》，頗見古今。

translations.literal: Through this he browsed the Records and the History and came to know something of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Through this he read the Records and the History and gained some knowledge of past and present.

sentences.zh: 演之門生朱重民入為主書，薦喜為主書書史，進為主圖令史。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's student Zhu Chongmin entered service as chief secretary; he recommended Xi as chief secretary's clerical officer, and [Xi] advanced to chief of the maps office.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's student Zhu Chongmin became chief secretary and recommended Xi as clerical officer to the chief secretary; Xi was later promoted to chief of the maps office.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗求圖書，喜開卷倒進之，太祖怒，遣出。

translations.literal: The Founder once sought books; Xi opened the scroll and handed it in upside down. The Founder was angry and sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked for books; Xi opened the scroll and presented it upside down. The emperor was furious and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 會太子步兵校尉沈慶之征蠻，啟太祖請喜自隨，使命去來，為世祖所知賞。

translations.literal: When Infantry Commandant Shen Qingzhi campaigned against the barbarians, he petitioned the Founder to let Xi follow him of his own accord; in missions going back and forth he came to be known and appreciated by Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: When Infantry Commandant Shen Qingzhi campaigned against the barbarians, he asked Emperor Wu to let Xi accompany him. On missions to and fro Xi won Emperor Xiaowu's notice and favor.

sentences.zh: 世祖於巴口建義，喜遇病，不堪隨慶之下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu raised the righteous army at the Ba crossing, Xi fell ill and could not follow Qingzhi south.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu launched the righteous rising at the Ba crossing, Xi fell ill and could not march south with Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 事平，世祖以喜為主書，稍見親遇，擢為諸王學官令，左右尚方令，河東太守，殿中御史。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Emperor Xiaowu made Xi chief secretary, gradually showed him favor, and promoted him to Instructor to the Princes, Left Attendant of the Inner Workshop, Administrator of Hedong, and Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After victory Emperor Xiaowu made him chief secretary, drew him close, and promoted him through instructor to the princes, left attendant of the inner workshop, administrator of Hedong, and palace censor.

sentences.zh: 大明中，黟、歙二縣有亡命數千人，攻破縣邑，殺害官長。

translations.literal: In the Daming era, in the two counties of Yi and She there were several thousand outlaws who broke through the county seats and killed the magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming reign, several thousand fugitives in Yi and She counties stormed the county seats and murdered the local officials.

sentences.zh: 豫章王子尚為揚州，在會稽，再遣主帥，領三千人水陸討伐；

translations.literal: Prince Zishang of Yuzhang held Yang Province and was at Kuaiji; he twice sent commanding generals leading three thousand men to suppress them by land and water;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, who governed Yang Province from Kuaiji, twice dispatched commanders with three thousand troops to attack them by land and sea;

sentences.zh: 遂再往，失利。

translations.literal: They then went twice more and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Both expeditions failed.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣喜將數十人至二縣，誘說群賊，賊即日歸降。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent Xi with several dozen men to the two counties to persuade the bandits, and the bandits surrendered that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu dispatched Wu Xi with a few dozen men to win over the rebels by persuasion, and the rebels submitted the same day.

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，四方反叛，東兵尤急。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first took the throne, rebellions broke out on all sides, and the eastern campaign was especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign, revolts erupted everywhere, and the crisis in the east was the most pressing.

sentences.zh: 喜請得精兵三百，致死於東，上大說，即假建武將軍，簡羽林勇士配之。

translations.literal: Xi asked for three hundred picked troops to fight to the death in the east; the emperor was greatly pleased and at once made him Acting General Who Establishes Might, selecting Palace Guard warriors to assign him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi requested three hundred elite soldiers and offered to stake his life in the east. The emperor was delighted, immediately granted him the acting title General Who Establishes Might, and picked crack troops from the Palace Guard to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 議者以喜刀筆主者，不嘗為將，不可遣。

translations.literal: Those who debated the matter held that Xi was a chief clerk with pen and knife, had never served as a general, and should not be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that Wu Xi was a desk officer who had never commanded troops and was unfit for the assignment.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人巢尚之曰：「喜昔隨沈慶之，屢經軍旅，性既勇決，又習戰陳，若能任之，必有成績。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Chao Shangzhi said: "In the past Xi followed Shen Qingzhi and repeatedly passed through military campaigns; his nature is bold and resolute, and he is practiced in battle formations—if he can be entrusted with the task, there will surely be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Chao Shangzhi said, "Wu Xi once served under Shen Qingzhi and saw repeated action. He is bold by nature and knows the battlefield. Put him in command and he will deliver results.

sentences.zh: 諸人紛紛，皆是不別才耳。」

translations.literal: The others' clamor is simply failure to distinguish talent."
translations.idiomatic: All this fuss is nothing but blindness to real ability."

sentences.zh: 喜乃率員外散騎侍郎竺超之、殿中將軍杜敬真馬步東討。

translations.literal: Xi then led Supernumerary Attendant Gentlemen of the Palace Dismounts Zhu Chaozhi and Palace General Du Jingzhen eastward to attack by horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi then marched east with Zhu Chaozhi, supernumerary attendant gentleman of the palace dismounts, and Palace General Du Jingzhen, campaigning by land and river.

sentences.zh: 既至永世，得庾業、劉延熙書，送尋陽王子房檄文。

translations.literal: When he reached Yongshi he obtained letters from Yu Ye and Liu Yanxi, together with a proclamation from Prince Zifang of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongshi he received letters from Yu Ye and Liu Yanxi along with a manifesto issued by Prince Zifang of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 與喜書曰：「知統戎旅，已次近路，卿所在著名，今日何為立忠於彼邪？

translations.literal: He wrote to Xi saying: "Knowing that you command the army and are already encamped on the near road—your name is famous wherever you are—why today do you stand in loyalty to them?
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Wu Xi: "I know you are leading the army and are already close at hand. Your reputation precedes you everywhere—so why do you now cast your loyalty with them?

sentences.zh: 想便倒戈，共受河、山之賞。」

translations.literal: I expect you will soon turn your spears about and together receive rewards of rivers and mountains."
translations.idiomatic: Surely you will turn your spears around at once and share with us the rewards of land and office."

sentences.zh: 喜報書曰：「前驅之人，忽獲來翰，披尋狂惑，良深悵駭。

translations.literal: Xi replied in a letter: "We who lead the van have suddenly received your written message; unfolding and reading it, I find it wildly deluded and am deeply shocked and dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi answered in a letter: "We in the vanguard have suddenly received your note. Reading this mad delusion, I am deeply appalled.

sentences.zh: 聖主以神武撥亂，德盛勳高，群逆交扇，滅在晷刻。

translations.literal: The sage ruler by divine martial prowess has quelled disorder; his virtue is abundant and his merit lofty—the rebellious masses fan one another, and their destruction is within a sunbeam's span.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage ruler has restored order by divine force of arms. His virtue towers and his merit is great. The rebels are fanning one another to ruin, and their end is only moments away.

sentences.zh: 君等勳義之烈，世荷國恩，事愧鳴鴞，不懷食椹。

translations.literal: You lords' merit and righteousness are illustrious; generation after generation you have borne the state's grace—your conduct shames the screech owl that eats mulberries without regard for its parent.
translations.idiomatic: Your houses have served with honor and long enjoyed the state's favor. Yet your deeds would shame the unfilial screech owl of the Odes—the bird that eats mulberries but never repays its nest.

sentences.zh: 今練勒所部，星言進邁，相見在近，不復多陳。」

translations.literal: Now I am drilling and mustering my command and will advance like a star—our meeting is close, so I will not say more."
translations.idiomatic: I am now drilling my troops and will march at once. We shall meet soon enough, and I need say no more."

sentences.zh: 喜，孝武世見驅使，常充使命，性寬厚，所至人並懷之。

translations.literal: Xi, during Emperor Xiaowu's reign, was constantly sent on missions; he was generous by nature, and wherever he went people all cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu, Wu Xi was often dispatched on imperial errands. He was warm by nature, and people everywhere came to trust him.

sentences.zh: 及東討，百姓聞吳河東來，便望風降散，故喜所至克捷，事在孔覬傳。

translations.literal: When he campaigned east, the common people heard that Wu Hedong was coming and at once scattered in surrender before the wind, so wherever Xi went he won victories—the details are in Kong Chong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: During the eastern campaign, the people heard that Wu Hedong was approaching and surrendered in droves before he even arrived. That is why Wu Xi met success wherever he went; the full account appears in Kong Chong's biography.

sentences.zh: 遷步兵校尉，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Infantry Commandant, his generalship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Infantry Commandant while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 封竟陵縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingling District with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Marquis of Jingling with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 東土平定，又率所領南討，遷輔國將軍、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: When the eastern territories were pacified, he again led his forces south to suppress rebellion and was promoted to General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the east was pacified, he led his troops south against the rebels and was appointed General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 南賊退走，喜追討平定荊州，遷前軍將軍，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When the southern rebels retreated and fled, Xi pursued, suppressed them, and pacified Jing Province; he was promoted to General of the Vanguard and his fief increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern rebels broke and fled, Wu Xi pursued them, crushed the revolt, and pacified Jing Province. He was made General of the Vanguard and his fief was increased by three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，改封東興縣侯，戶邑如先。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing District, his households and fief as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi his title was changed to Marquis of Dongxing, with the same fief as before.

sentences.zh: 仍除使持節、督交州、廣州之鬱林、寧浦二郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of all military affairs in Yulin and Ningpu commanderies of Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was next named bearer of the staff of authority, supervisor of military affairs in Yulin and Ningpu of Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 不行，又除右軍將軍、淮陵太守，假輔師將軍，兼太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He did not go; he was instead appointed General of the Right, Administrator of Huailing, Acting General Who Assists the Army, and concurrently Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He never took up the Jiao post. Instead he was made General of the Right and Administrator of Huailing, with the acting title General Who Assists the Army and concurrent appointment as Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉驍騎將軍，假號、太守、兼率如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry; his acting rank, administrator's post, and concurrent commandancy remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, keeping his acting title, prefecture, and concurrent guard command.

sentences.zh: 其年，虜寇豫州，喜統諸軍出討，大破虜於荊亭，偽長社公遁走，戍主帛乞奴歸降。

translations.literal: That year the barbarians raided Yu Province; Xi commanded the armies in an expedition and routed them at Jingting; the false Duke of Changshe fled, and the garrison commander Bo Qinu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: That year the enemy raided Yu Province. Wu Xi took command of the expeditionary force and inflicted a crushing defeat on them at Jingting. The Wei pretender Duke of Changshe fled, and the garrison commander Bo Qinu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 軍還，復以本位兼左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he again held his original rank while concurrently serving as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he resumed his former rank while also serving as General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 六年，又率軍向豫州拒索虜，加節、督豫州諸軍事，假冠軍將軍，驍騎、太守如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again led the army toward Yu Province to resist the Northern Wei enemies, was granted the staff of authority and made Supervisor of all military affairs in Yu Province, Acting General Who Conquers the Enemy; his cavalry generalship and administrator's post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he marched again toward Yu Province to hold off the Northern Wei invaders. He received the staff of authority, was made supervisor of Yu Province military affairs and Acting General Who Conquers the Enemy, and kept his cavalry title and prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，還京都。

translations.literal: The next year he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，喜東征，白太宗得尋陽王子房及諸賊帥，即於東梟斬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xi set out east, he reported to Emperor Ming that if he captured Prince Zifang of Xunyang and the rebel chiefs he would at once have them displayed and beheaded in the east.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi first marched east, he had told Emperor Ming that once he captured Prince Zifang of Xunyang and the rebel leaders, he would execute them on the spot in the east.

sentences.zh: 東土既平，喜見南賊方熾，慮後翻覆受禍，乃生送子房還都；

translations.literal: When the eastern territories were pacified, Xi saw that the southern rebels were still blazing fierce; fearing later reversal and suffering harm, he sent Prince Zifang alive back to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: After the east was pacified, Wu Xi saw the southern rebellion still raging. Fearing a later reversal that would destroy him, he sent Prince Zifang back to the capital alive;

sentences.zh: 凡諸大主帥顧琛、王曇生之徒，皆被全活。

translations.literal: All the great commanders such as Gu Chen and Wang Tansheng were fully spared and kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: and he spared the lives of major rebel commanders such as Gu Chen and Wang Tansheng.

sentences.zh: 上以喜新立大功，不問也，而內密銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xi had just won great merit, did not pursue the matter, but secretly harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wu Xi had just won a great victory, the emperor let the matter pass publicly but secretly nursed a grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 及平荊州，恣意剽虜，贓私萬計；

translations.literal: When Jing Province was pacified he plundered at will, and his illicit gains numbered in the tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: After Jing Province was subdued, he looted without restraint, amassing private wealth beyond counting;

sentences.zh: 又嘗對賓客言漢高、魏武本是何人，上聞之，益不說。

translations.literal: He also once said before guests who Han Gaozu and Wei Wu really were; when the emperor heard of this he was all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: and he once remarked before guests about what sort of men Han Gaozu and Wei Wu really were. When the emperor heard of it, his displeasure only deepened.

sentences.zh: 其後誅壽寂之，喜內懼，因啟乞中散大夫，上尤疑駭。

translations.literal: Afterward, when Shou Jizhi was executed, Xi inwardly feared and petitioned for the post of Palace Gentleman for Regular Attendance; the emperor was especially suspicious and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Shou Jizhi was put to death, Wu Xi grew afraid and petitioned to be made Palace Gentleman for Regular Attendance. The emperor was especially suspicious and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 至是會上有疾，為身後之慮，以喜素得人情，疑其將來不能事幼主，乃賜死，時年四十五。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor happened to be ill; thinking of what would come after his death, and because Xi had always won people's hearts, he suspected that in the future Xi would not be able to serve the young ruler—so he was granted death by poison; he was forty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor fell ill and began planning for the succession. Wu Xi had always been popular, and the emperor feared he would not loyally serve the young heir. He was therefore ordered to take poison. Wu Xi was forty-five.

sentences.zh: 喜將死之日，上召入內殿與共言謔，酬接甚款。

translations.literal: On the day Xi was about to die, the emperor summoned him into the inner hall and exchanged banter with him; their interaction was very cordial.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Wu Xi was to die, the emperor summoned him to the inner hall and joked with him in an unusually warm and friendly manner.

sentences.zh: 既出，賜以名饌，并金銀御器，敕將命者勿使食器宿喜家。

translations.literal: After he came out he was granted famous delicacies together with gold and silver imperial utensils, and the emperor ordered the envoy not to let the eating vessels remain overnight in Xi's home.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi left, the emperor gave him fine food and gold and silver imperial tableware, and ordered the messenger not to leave those vessels overnight in Wu Xi's house.

sentences.zh: 上素多忌諱，不欲令食器停凶禍之室故也。

translations.literal: The emperor had always been very superstitious and did not want the eating vessels to remain in a room of ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply superstitious and refused to let imperial vessels stay in a house touched by violent death.

sentences.zh: 喜未死一日，上與劉勔、張興世、齊王詔曰：

translations.literal: One day before Xi died, the emperor addressed Liu Yan, Zhang Xingshi, and the Prince of Qi, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the day before Wu Xi's death, the emperor summoned Liu Yan, Zhang Xingshi, and the Prince of Qi and said:

sentences.zh: 吳喜出自卑寒，少被驅使，利口任詐，輕狡萬端。

translations.literal: "Wu Xi came from lowly, humble origins; in youth he was driven about as a servant—glib of tongue and trusting in trickery, frivolous and cunning in ten thousand ways.
translations.idiomatic: "Wu Xi was born in poverty and spent his youth as a menial runner. He is quick with words and reckless with deceit, slippery and scheming in every conceivable way.

sentences.zh: 自元嘉以來，便充刀筆小役，賣弄威恩，苟取物情，處處交結，皆為黨與，眾中常以正直為詞，而內實阿媚。

translations.literal: Since the Yuanjia era he has served in petty clerk duties, trading on power and favor, currying popular sentiment; everywhere he formed connections—all became factional allies. In public he always spoke of uprightness, but inwardly he was fawning.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yuanjia era he has filled minor clerk posts, playing power and favor for all they are worth and courting popularity wherever he goes. He has woven a web of partisans, yet in public he poses as upright while privately fawning on whoever serves his interest.

sentences.zh: 每仗計數，運其佞巧，甘言說色，曲以事人，不忠不平，彰於觸事。

translations.literal: He always relied on schemes, deploying his sycophantic cleverness—sweet words and pleasing looks, bending to serve others. Disloyalty and unfairness showed clearly whenever affairs arose.
translations.idiomatic: He lives by calculation, deploying flattery and charm—honeyed speech, obliging manner, and servile accommodation. His disloyalty and injustice show themselves the moment any matter is tested.

sentences.zh: 從來作諸署，主意所不協者，覓罪委頓之，以示清直；

translations.literal: Whenever he served in various offices, anyone the chief opposed, he would find fault and bring down to show himself upright;
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held, if the chief disliked someone, Wu Xi would hunt out a charge and ruin that man to burnish his own reputation for integrity;

sentences.zh: 而餘人恣意為非，一不檢問，故甚得物情。

translations.literal: Yet when others wantonly did wrong he never once investigated—thus he won great popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: yet when others ran wild he never checked them at all. That is how he won such broad popularity.

sentences.zh: 昔大明中，黟、歙二縣有亡命數千人，攻破縣邑，殺害官長。

translations.literal: In the past during the Daming era, in Yi and She counties several thousand outlaws broke through county seats and killed magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era, several thousand outlaws in Yi and She counties overran the county seats and murdered the officials.

sentences.zh: 劉子尚在會稽，再遣為主帥，領三千精甲水陸討伐，再往失利。

translations.literal: Liu Zishang was at Kuaiji and twice sent commanders with three thousand elite troops to suppress them by land and water; twice they went and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zishang, stationed at Kuaiji, twice sent commanders with three thousand picked troops against them by land and water, and both campaigns failed.

sentences.zh: 孝武以喜將數十人至二縣說誘群賊，賊即歸降。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent Xi with several dozen men to the two counties to persuade the bandits, and the bandits at once surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu then sent Wu Xi with a few dozen men to talk the rebels into submission, and they surrendered immediately.

sentences.zh: 詭數幻惑，乃能如此，故每豫驅馳，窮諸狡慝。

translations.literal: By deceitful schemes and illusions he could do such things—therefore he was constantly sent hurrying about, exhausting every sort of treacherous villainy.
translations.idiomatic: By trickery and illusion he could produce results like that, which is why he was always dispatched on urgent errands—to squeeze every kind of cunning malice out of him.

sentences.zh: 及泰始初東討，正有三百人，直造三吳，凡再經薄戰，而自破岡以東至海十郡，無不清蕩。

translations.literal: When the eastern campaign began at the start of Taishi, he had only three hundred men, drove straight into the Three Wu region, passed through two light battles, and from Po Hill eastward to the sea—ten commanderies—none were not cleared.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taishi eastern campaign he had only three hundred men, yet he drove straight into the Three Wu, fought only two minor engagements, and cleared ten commanderies from Broken Hill east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞吳河東來，便望風自退，若非積取三吳人情，何以得弭伏如此。

translations.literal: When the common people heard Wu Hedong was coming they retreated before the wind by themselves—if he had not long accumulated favor in the Three Wu, how could he have obtained such quiet submission?
translations.idiomatic: The people heard that Wu Hedong was coming and melted away without a fight. Without years of currying favor in the Three Wu, how could he have pacified the region so easily?

sentences.zh: 其統軍寬慢無章，放恣諸將，無所裁檢，故部曲為之致力。

translations.literal: His command of the army was lax and without discipline; he let the generals run wild and restrained nothing—therefore his troops exerted themselves for him.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded with slack discipline, giving his officers free rein and checking almost nothing. That is why his men fought so hard for him personally.

sentences.zh: 觀其意趣，止在賊平之後，應力為國計。

translations.literal: Judging his intent, it was only after the bandits were pacified that he should have exerted himself for the state's interest.
translations.idiomatic: But look at what he really wanted: once the rebels were down, he should have thrown himself into the state's service. Instead he had other plans.

sentences.zh: 喜初東徵發都，指天畫地，云得劉子房即當屏除，袁標等皆加斬戮，使略無生口。

translations.literal: When Xi first set out on the eastern campaign from the capital, he pointed to heaven and traced the earth, declaring that once he got Liu Zifang he would immediately eliminate him, and Yuan Biao and the rest would all be beheaded, leaving hardly a living mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi left the capital on the eastern campaign, he swore by heaven and earth that if he captured Prince Zifang he would kill him at once, along with Yuan Biao and the rest, leaving scarcely a survivor.

sentences.zh: 既平之後，緩兵施恩，納罪人之貨，誘諸賊帥，令各逃藏，受賂得物，不可稱紀。

translations.literal: After pacification he slowed the army and dispensed favors, accepting the goods of criminals, enticing the rebel chiefs to hide themselves separately—the bribes and goods received cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Once victory was won, he slowed his advance and traded favors for loot, taking bribes from condemned men and helping rebel chiefs slip away and hide. The goods he accepted cannot even be reckoned.

sentences.zh: 聽諸賊帥假稱為降，而擁衛子房遂得生歸朝庭。

translations.literal: He let the rebel chiefs pretend to surrender while escorting Zifang, who thus was able to return alive to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He let the rebel leaders fake their submission while escorting Prince Zifang safely back to court alive.

sentences.zh: 收羅群逆，皆作爪牙，撫接優密，過於義士。

translations.literal: He gathered all the rebels and made them his agents; he treated and received them with intimate favor exceeding that shown to loyal men.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the rebels around him and made them his personal agents, treating them with a warmth he never showed loyal officers.

sentences.zh: 推此意，正是聞南賊大盛，殷孝祖戰亡，人情大惡，慮逆徒得志，規以自免。

translations.literal: Inferring from this intent, it was precisely that hearing the southern rebels were in great strength, Yin Xiaozu had died in battle, popular sentiment was greatly hostile, and fearing the rebels would prevail, he planned to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning is plain: when he heard the southern revolt was surging, that Yin Xiaozu had fallen in battle, and that public morale had collapsed, he feared the rebels might win and began arranging his own escape.

sentences.zh: 喜善為姦變，每以計數自將，於朝廷則三吳首獻慶捷，於南賊則不殺其黨，頗著陰誠。

translations.literal: Xi is skilled at treacherous shifts; he always led himself by schemes—toward the court he was first to present victory reports from the Three Wu, toward the southern rebels he did not kill their partisans, showing considerable secret loyalty to them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi is a master of double-dealing. He always ran his own game: to the court he was first with victory dispatches from the Three Wu, but toward the southern rebels he spared their followers and showed them unmistakable private loyalty.

sentences.zh: 當云東人恇怯，望風自散，皆是彼無處分，非其苦相逼迫，保全子房及顧琛等，足表丹誠，進退二塗，可以無患。

translations.literal: He would say the eastern men were timid and cowardly and scattered before the wind—yet none of that was due to their lack of disposition; they were not harshly pressed. Saving Zifang and Gu Chen and the rest fully showed his sincere devotion to the rebels; with two paths of advance and retreat he could be free from worry.
translations.idiomatic: He could claim the easterners were cowards who fled at a rumor, but in truth they were not broken by force. By preserving Prince Zifang, Gu Chen, and the others he proved where his real loyalty lay. With a path forward and a path back, he thought himself safe either way.

sentences.zh: 南賊未平，唯以軍糧為急，西南及北道斷不通，東土新平，商運稀簡，朝廷乃至鬻官賣爵，以救災困，斗斛收斂，猶有不充。

translations.literal: The southern rebels were not yet pacified and military grain was the sole urgency; southwest and northern routes were cut and impassable, the eastern territory was newly pacified, and merchant transport was sparse—the court even sold offices and ranks to relieve disaster and hardship, yet collecting grain by the peck still fell short.
translations.idiomatic: The southern rebellion was still unresolved and grain was the one desperate need. Routes to the southwest and north were severed, the east had only just been pacified, and commerce was thin. The court was even selling offices and titles to stave off famine, yet every bushel collected still fell short.

sentences.zh: 喜在赭圻，軍主者頓偷一百三十斛米，初不問罪；

translations.literal: When Xi was at Zheqi, a unit commander secretly stole one hundred thirty hu of grain, and at first Xi did not question the crime;
translations.idiomatic: At Zheqi, one of Wu Xi's unit commanders stole one hundred thirty hu of grain, and Wu Xi at first refused even to investigate;

sentences.zh: 諸軍主皆云宜治，喜不獲已，止與三十鞭，又不責備，凡所曲意，類皆如此。

translations.literal: All the unit commanders said he should be punished; Xi, having no choice, gave only thirty lashes and did not hold him accountable—everything he indulged followed this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: when every other commander insisted on punishment, Wu Xi reluctantly gave the man thirty strokes and let the matter drop. That is how he indulged wrongdoing across the board.

sentences.zh: 喜至荊州，公私殷富，錢物無復孑遺。

translations.literal: When Xi reached Jing Province, public and private wealth was abundant, yet not a single coin or thing was left.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Wu Xi reached Jing Province, a region rich in public and private wealth, he had stripped it bare.

sentences.zh: 喜乘兵威之盛，誅求推檢，凡所課責，既無定科，又嚴令驅蹙，皆使立辦。

translations.literal: Xi took advantage of the army's might to extort and investigate; every levy and exaction had no fixed rule, and under strict orders to drive and squeeze all had to be provided on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He used military power to extort and audit the province. His levies had no fixed scale, and under harsh orders to squeeze every source, everything had to be delivered at once.

sentences.zh: 所使之人，莫非姦猾。

translations.literal: Those he employed were none but cunning scoundrels.
translations.idiomatic: The men he sent out were all sharp operators and thieves.

sentences.zh: 因公行私，迫脅在所。

translations.literal: Using public business to pursue private gain, they coerced whoever was at hand.
translations.idiomatic: They abused official business for private profit and bullied everyone they encountered.

sentences.zh: 入官之物，侵竊過半。

translations.literal: Of goods that entered the public store, more than half was embezzled.
translations.idiomatic: More than half of what was supposed to enter the public coffers never got there.

sentences.zh: 納資請託，不知猒已。

translations.literal: Accepting payments and grant of favors, he did not know satiety.
translations.idiomatic: He took bribes and traded favors without ever knowing when to stop.

sentences.zh: 西難既殄，便應還朝，而解故盤停，託云捍蜀。

translations.literal: Once the western crisis was extinguished he should have returned to court, but he dismissed his old troops and lingered, claiming to guard against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Once the western threat was crushed he should have returned to court, but he kept his army in place and lingered on, claiming he was holding the line against Shu.

sentences.zh: 實由貨易交關，事未回展。

translations.literal: In truth it was because trade and commercial dealings were not yet completed.
translations.idiomatic: In truth he was waiting to finish his business deals.

sentences.zh: 又遣人入蠻，矯詔慰勞，賧伐所得，一以入私。

translations.literal: He also sent men into the barbarian lands with forged imperial edicts of consolation and reward, putting all proceeds from tribute and conquest into private hands.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent agents into the tribal lands with forged imperial edicts of reward, and kept every penny of tribute and booty for himself.

sentences.zh: 又遣部下將吏，兼因土地富人，往襄陽或蜀、漢，屬託郡縣，侵官害民，興生求利，千端萬緒。

translations.literal: He also sent subordinate officers, drawing on local wealthy men, to Xiangyang or Shu and Han to entrust county magistrates, encroach on offices, harm the people, and pursue profit in every imaginable way.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched subordinates, backed by local magnates, to Xiangyang and to Shu and Han to lean on county officials, abuse public office, prey on the people, and chase profit by every possible means.

sentences.zh: 從西還，大艑小艒，爰及草舫，錢米布絹，無船不滿。

translations.literal: Returning from the west, great barges and small boats, even grass craft—money, grain, cloth, silk—not one vessel was unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: On the return from the west, great barges and small boats—even reed rafts—were loaded with money, grain, cloth, and silk. Not one craft sailed empty.

sentences.zh: 自喜以下，迨至小將，人人重載，莫不兼資。

translations.literal: From Xi down to the junior officers, every man carried a heavy load, all without exception enriched.
translations.idiomatic: From Wu Xi himself down to the lowest officers, every man came back weighed down with loot. None returned poor.

sentences.zh: 喜本小人，多被使役，經由水陸，州郡殆遍；

translations.literal: Xi was originally a petty man, often sent on missions; traveling by water and land he had covered nearly every province and commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi began as a low-born runner who was constantly sent on errands. By land and water he had passed through nearly every province;

sentences.zh: 所至之處，輒結物情，妄竊善稱。

translations.literal: wherever he went he would cultivate popular sentiment and falsely steal a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: and wherever he went he cultivated local goodwill and built himself an undeserved name for virtue.

sentences.zh: 聲滿天下，密懷姦惡，人莫之知。

translations.literal: His fame filled the realm, yet he secretly harbored treacherous evil—no one knew it.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation rang across the empire, yet beneath it he nursed treachery that almost no one saw.

sentences.zh: 喜軍中諸將，非劫便賊，唯云：「賊何須殺，但取之，必得其用。」

translations.literal: Xi's officers in the army were either robbers or bandits, and he would only say: "Why need bandits be killed? Just take them—you are sure to get use from them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's commanders were mostly robbers or former rebels themselves, and he would say only this: "Why kill bandits at all? Capture them and they will serve you well.

sentences.zh: 雖復羸弱，亦言：「健兒可惜，天下未平，但令以功贖罪。」

translations.literal: Even if they were weak, he would also say: "What a pity to waste brave men—the realm is not yet pacified; just let them redeem their crimes through merit.
translations.idiomatic: Even when they were weaklings, he would add: "Good fighting men are too precious to waste while the realm is still unsettled. Let them buy pardon with service.

sentences.zh: 處遇料理，反勝勞人，此輩所感唯喜，莫云恩由朝廷。

translations.literal: His handling and care for them actually surpassed that given to loyal men; these men felt gratitude only toward Xi, and never said the grace came from the court.
translations.idiomatic: He treated them better than he treated loyal soldiers. They owed their gratitude to Wu Xi alone and never credited the throne.

sentences.zh: 兇惡不革，恆出醜聲，勞人義士，相與歎息，並云：「我等不愛性命，擊擒此賊，朝廷不肯殺去，反與我齊。

translations.literal: His vicious wickedness was unchanged and ugly talk constantly issued; loyal men sighed together and all said: "We do not spare our lives—we strike and capture these bandits, yet the court will not have them killed but ranks them alongside us.
translations.idiomatic: His cruelty never changed, and foul complaints kept pouring out. Loyal soldiers groaned among themselves and said, "We risk our lives to capture these rebels, and the court will not execute them—it ranks them with us instead.

sentences.zh: 今天下若更有賊，我不復能擊也。」

translations.literal: If there are bandits again in the realm, we can no longer bring ourselves to fight them."
translations.idiomatic: If bandits rise again in this empire, we will not lift a hand against them."

sentences.zh: 此等既隨喜行，多無功效，或隱在眾後，或在幔屋中眠。

translations.literal: These men who followed Xi were mostly useless; some hid behind the ranks or slept in the tent pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: The men Wu Xi kept around him were mostly dead weight. Some hid at the rear of the column; others slept in the tent pavilions.

sentences.zh: 賊即破散，與勞人同受爵賞。

translations.literal: When the bandits were routed and scattered they received ranks and rewards together with the loyal men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once the rebels broke, they received the same honors and rewards as the men who had actually fought.

sentences.zh: 既被詰問，辭白百端，云：「此輩既見原宥，擊賊有功，那得不依例加賞。」

translations.literal: When questioned, he had a hundred excuses, saying: "Since these men were pardoned and had merit fighting bandits, how could rewards not be granted according to rule?
translations.idiomatic: When challenged, he had endless excuses: "These men were pardoned and then fought well. How could I refuse them rewards by the usual rule?

sentences.zh: 褚淵往南選諸將卒，喜為軍中經為賊者，就淵求官，倍於義士。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan went south to select officers and soldiers; Xi interceded for those in the army who had been bandits to seek offices from Yuan, twice as many as for loyal men.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Yuan went south to review the troops, Wu Xi pressed him to grant offices to former bandits in the army—twice as many petitions as he made for loyal men.

sentences.zh: 淵以喜最前獻捷，名位已通，又為統副，難相違拒，是以得官受賞，反多義人。

translations.literal: Yuan, because Xi had been first to report victory, already held rank and position, and was also the army's deputy commander, found it hard to refuse—thus those who gained offices and rewards were, on the contrary, more numerous than the loyal men.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan, unable to refuse Wu Xi—who had reported victory first, already held high rank, and served as army deputy—ended up giving offices and rewards disproportionately to the wrong men rather than to the loyal soldiers.

sentences.zh: 義人雖忿喜不平，又懷其寬弛。

translations.literal: The loyal men, though resentful of Xi's unfairness, also cherished his leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal troops resented Wu Xi's injustice, yet they also came to rely on his laxness.

sentences.zh: 往歲竺超之聞四方反叛，人情畏賊，無敢求為朝廷行者，乃慨然攘步，隨喜出征，為其軍副。

translations.literal: In past years when Zhu Chaozhi heard of rebellions on all sides and popular sentiment feared the bandits, with none daring to volunteer for the court, he resolutely stepped forward and followed Xi on campaign as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years, when rebellions erupted everywhere and men were afraid even to march for the throne, Zhu Chaozhi stepped forward of his own accord and joined Wu Xi's campaign as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 身經臨敵，自東還，失喜意。

translations.literal: He personally faced the enemy in battle, yet when he returned from the east he lost Xi's favor.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the front lines himself, yet when he came back from the east he had fallen out of Wu Xi's favor.

sentences.zh: 說超之多酒，不堪驅使，遂相委棄。

translations.literal: Xi said Chaozhi drank too much and could not be driven to service, and so abandoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi claimed Chaozhi drank too heavily to be of use and cast him aside.

sentences.zh: 高敬祖年雖少宿，氣力實健，其有處分，為軍中所稱，喜薄其衰老，云無所施。

translations.literal: Gao Jingzu, though advanced in years, was in truth strong in vitality; his dispositions were praised in the army, yet Xi belittled him as senile, saying there was nothing to which he could be put.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jingzu was older but still vigorous, and the army respected his judgment. Wu Xi dismissed him as worn out and declared him useless.

sentences.zh: 正以二人忠清，與己異行。

translations.literal: It was precisely because the two men were loyal and upright, of a different conduct from his own.
translations.idiomatic: He did this only because both men were honest and upright—nothing like him.

sentences.zh: 超之為人，乃多飲酒，計喜軍中主帥，豈無飲酒者？

translations.literal: As for Chaozhi's character, it is true he drank much—but consider: among the commanders in Xi's army, were there none who drank?
translations.idiomatic: It is true that Chaozhi drank, but were there no other drinking commanders in Wu Xi's army?

sentences.zh: 特是不利超之，故以酒致言耳。

translations.literal: It was simply that Chaozhi was not to his advantage, so he used drink as an excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi simply found Chaozhi inconvenient, and used wine as a pretext to get rid of him.

sentences.zh: 敬祖既無餘事，直云年老，託為乞郡，潛相遣斥。

translations.literal: Jingzu had no other fault; Xi simply cited old age, feigned granting him a requested prefecture, and secretly had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jingzu had done nothing wrong. Wu Xi cited his age, pretended to grant the prefecture he had requested, and quietly pushed him out.

sentences.zh: 其餘主帥，並貪濁謅媚之流，皆提攜東西，不相離捨。

translations.literal: The other commanders were all of the greedy, corrupt, and fawning sort; each carried the other's fortunes to and fro and never parted.
translations.idiomatic: His other commanders were greedy, corrupt sycophants who looked out for one another at every turn and never broke ranks.

sentences.zh: 喜聞天壤間有罪人死或應繫者，必啟以入軍，皆得官爵，厚被處遇。

translations.literal: When Xi heard that anywhere under heaven there were criminals due for death or imprisonment, he would invariably report them for entry into the army; all received offices and titles and were richly treated.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wu Xi learned of a condemned or imprisoned criminal anywhere in the realm, he would recommend the man for the army. Each one received rank and title and lavish treatment.

sentences.zh: 應入死之人，緣己得活，非唯得活，又復如意。

translations.literal: Those who should have entered death, through him obtained life—not only obtaining life but also obtaining their wishes besides.
translations.idiomatic: Men who should have been executed owed their lives to him; they not only kept their lives but got whatever they wanted besides.

sentences.zh: 人非木石，何能不感！

translations.literal: Men are not wood or stone; how could they not be moved!
translations.idiomatic: Human beings are not made of wood or stone. How could they not feel grateful!

sentences.zh: 設令吾攻喜門，此輩誰不致力，但是喜不敢生心耳。

translations.literal: Suppose I attacked Xi's gate—these men, who would not exert themselves? It is only that Xi does not dare conceive the thought.
translations.idiomatic: If I attacked Wu Xi's own command, every one of these men would fight for him—it is only that Xi has not yet dared to turn on me.

sentences.zh: 喜軍中人皆是喜身爪牙，豈關於國。

translations.literal: The men in Xi's army are all Xi's personal claws and teeth—what have they to do with the state?
translations.idiomatic: The men in Wu Xi's army are his private henchmen, not servants of the throne.

sentences.zh: 喜自得軍號以來，多置吏佐，是人加板，無復限極。

translations.literal: Since Xi obtained his military commission, he has placed many clerks and assistants; every person receives an official tablet, with no further limit.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wu Xi received his military commission, he has packed his staff with aides. Each man gets an official appointment, with no end to it.

sentences.zh: 為兄弟子姪及其同堂群從，乞東名縣，連城四五，皆灼然巧盜，侵官奪私。

translations.literal: For his brothers, sons, nephews, and all their male cousins of the same hall, he petitioned for renowned eastern counties, four or five cities in succession—all clearly clever theft, encroaching on official lands and seizing private holdings.
translations.idiomatic: He secured famous counties in the east for his brothers, sons, nephews, and male cousins—four or five cities in a row—each grant a naked seizure of public and private property alike.

sentences.zh: 亡命罪人，州郡不得討；

translations.literal: Fugitive criminals—prefectures and commanderies could not pursue them;
translations.idiomatic: Fugitive criminals could not be pursued by the prefectures and commanderies;

sentences.zh: 崎嶇蔽匿，必也黨護。

translations.literal: Hiding in rugged concealment, they were inevitably protected by his clique.
translations.idiomatic: When they fled to rough country and hid, his faction always sheltered them.

sentences.zh: 臺州符旨，殆不復行。

translations.literal: Orders from the capital and the province scarcely received enforcement anymore.
translations.idiomatic: Orders from the capital and provincial authorities were barely obeyed at all.

sentences.zh: 船車牛犢，應為公家所假借者，託之於喜，吏司便不敢問。

translations.literal: Boats, carts, oxen, and calves that should have been borrowed for public use were entrusted to Xi, and the clerical offices did not dare to question it.
translations.idiomatic: Public boats, wagons, oxen, and calves were placed under Wu Xi's name, and no clerk dared challenge it.

sentences.zh: 它縣奴婢，入界便略。

translations.literal: Slaves and servants from other counties, upon entering his territory, were immediately seized.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves from neighboring counties were seized the moment they entered his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 百姓牛犢，輒索殺噉。

translations.literal: The common people's oxen and calves were invariably seized, killed, and eaten.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners' cattle strayed near, his men seized them, slaughtered them, and ate them.

sentences.zh: 州郡應及役者，竝入喜家。

translations.literal: Those in prefectures and commanderies due for corvée service all entered Xi's household.
translations.idiomatic: Every man in the district owed to corvée labor was placed in Wu Xi's household.

sentences.zh: 喜兄茹公等悉下取錢，盈村滿里。

translations.literal: Xi's elder brother Ru and the others all sent men down to collect money, filling every village and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's elder brother Ru and his kin sent men to squeeze money from the countryside until every village and hamlet groaned under it.

sentences.zh: 諸吳姻親，就人間徵求，無復紀極，百姓嗷然，人人悉苦。

translations.literal: All Wu kin by marriage made demands upon the people with no further measure; the people cried out, and every man suffered.
translations.idiomatic: His Wu in-laws preyed upon the people without limit. The countryside groaned, and everyone suffered.

sentences.zh: 喜具知此，初不禁呵。

translations.literal: Xi fully knew all of this, yet from the first did not forbid or reprove it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi knew all of this perfectly well and did nothing to stop it.

sentences.zh: 索惠子罪不甚江悆，既已被恩，得免憲辟，小小忤意，輒加刑斬。

translations.literal: Suo Huizi's crimes were not as serious as Jiang Yu's; having already received favor and escaped legal punishment, for the slightest offense he would apply execution.
