translations.idiomatic: Suo Huizi's offenses were lighter than Jiang Yu's. Wu Xi had already spared him once, yet punished the smallest slight with execution.

sentences.zh: 張悅賊中大帥，逼迫歸降，沈攸之錄付喜，云：「殺活當由朝廷。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yue was a great commander among the rebels; compelled to surrender, Shen Youzhi handed him over to Xi, saying: "Whether he lives or dies should be decided by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue had been a rebel commander. Shen Youzhi forced his surrender and delivered him to Wu Xi, saying, "Only the court may decide whether this man lives or dies.

sentences.zh: 將帥征伐，既有常體，自應執歸之有司。

translations.literal: Generals on campaign have their established form; one should naturally take captives bound to the competent offices.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders on campaign follow fixed procedure. Prisoners should be bound and handed to the proper authorities.

sentences.zh: 喜即便打鏁，解襦與著，對膝圍棋，仍造重義，私惠招物，觸事如斯。

translations.literal: Xi immediately had the shackles struck off, removed the inner robe and dressed him, played go knee-to-knee with him, further forged heavy obligations, used private favors to win men—every matter was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi had the shackles struck off at once, gave the man fresh clothes, and played go with him knee to knee. He built private loyalties and bought goodwill at every turn—this was his way in everything.

sentences.zh: 張靈度凶愚小人，背叛之首，喜在西輒恕其罪，私將下都，與之周旋，情若同體。

translations.literal: Zhang Lingdu was a vicious and stupid little man, head of the betrayal; in the west Xi repeatedly pardoned his crimes, secretly brought him down to the capital, associated with him, and was intimate as if of one body.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lingdu, a vicious fool who had led the rebellion, was repeatedly pardoned by Wu Xi in the west. Xi secretly brought him to the capital and kept him close, as if they shared one body.

sentences.zh: 狼子野心，獨懷毒性，遂與柳欣慰等謀立劉禕。

translations.literal: A wolf cub's wild heart—he alone nursed poison—and so with Liu Xinwei and others plotted to install Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Nursing wolfish ambitions and deadly malice, he joined Liu Xinwei and others in a plot to set up Liu Yi as emperor.

sentences.zh: 吾使喜錄之，而喜密報令去，去未得遠，為建康所錄。

translations.literal: I ordered Xi to arrest him, but Xi secretly reported to him to flee; he had not gone far before being arrested at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: I ordered Wu Xi to arrest him, but Xi secretly warned the man to flee. He had not gone far before Jiankang authorities captured him.

sentences.zh: 喜背國親惡，乃至於是。

translations.literal: Xi's betrayal of the state and closeness to evil reached even to this.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's betrayal of the state and embrace of evil went as far as this.

sentences.zh: 初從西反，圖兼右丞，貪因事物，以行私詐。

translations.literal: When he first returned from the west, he plotted to hold concurrently the right vice-directorship; greedily using every affair, he carried out private fraud.
translations.idiomatic: On first returning from the west, he angled for the concurrent post of Right Vice Director and used every official matter for private fraud.

sentences.zh: 吾患其諂曲，抑而不許，從此怨懟，意用不平。

translations.literal: I feared his sycophantic crookedness and suppressed him without granting it; from then on he nursed resentment, and his mind was never at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I distrusted his sycophantic ways and refused the appointment. From that point he harbored resentment and never felt settled.

sentences.zh: 喜西救汝陰，縱肆兵將，掠暴居民，姦人婦女，逼奪雞犬，虜略縱橫，緣路官長，莫敢呵問。

translations.literal: When Xi went west to rescue Ruyin, he let his troops and generals run wild, plundering and brutalizing residents, violating women, seizing chickens and dogs; looting ran rampant, and magistrates along the route dared not rebuke or question them.
translations.idiomatic: On his western relief march to Ruyin, Wu Xi let his soldiers run wild—plundering towns, raping women, stealing livestock—while local officials along the route dared not interfere.

sentences.zh: 脫誤有縛錄一人，喜輒大怒。

translations.literal: If by accident someone was bound and arrested, Xi would immediately fly into great anger.
translations.idiomatic: If any official accidentally arrested one of his men, Wu Xi flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 百姓呼嗟，人人失望。

translations.literal: The common people cried out in lament; every man lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned in despair; everyone lost faith in him.

sentences.zh: 近段佛榮求還，乃欲用喜代之。

translations.literal: Recently Duan Furong requested to return, and the plan was to use Xi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Furong recently asked to return home, the court planned to send Wu Xi to replace him.

sentences.zh: 西人聞其當來，皆欲叛走，云：「吳軍中人皆是生劫，若作刺史，吾等豈有活路。

translations.literal: When the western people heard he was coming, all wished to rebel and flee, saying: "The men in Wu's army are all born robbers—if he becomes prefect, how can we have any way to live?
translations.idiomatic: When the people in the west learned he was coming, they wanted to rebel and flee, saying, "Wu Xi's soldiers are born bandits. If he becomes our prefect, we have no way to survive.

sentences.zh: 既無他計，正當叛投虜耳。」

translations.literal: Having no other plan, we can only rebel and defect to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: We have no other choice but to rebel and join the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 夫伐罪弔民，用清國道。

translations.literal: To punish crime and comfort the people is to cleanse the nation's way.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing the guilty and comforting the people is how a ruler clears the path of state.

sentences.zh: 豈有殘虐無辜，剝奪為務，害政妨國，罔上附下，罪釁若此，而可久容！

translations.literal: How can there be one who cruelly abuses the innocent, makes plunder his task, harms governance and obstructs the state, deceives the sovereign above and attaches himself to the base below, with crimes like these—and yet be long tolerated!
translations.idiomatic: How could the throne long tolerate a man who brutalizes innocents, lives by plunder, corrupts government, deceives his superiors, panders to his followers, and commits crimes like these!

sentences.zh: 臧文仲有云：「見有善於其君，如孝子之養父母；

translations.literal: Zang Wenzhong said: "When one sees what is good for one's lord, one should serve it as a filial son nourishes his parents;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wenzhong once said, "When you see something that will benefit your lord, tend it as a filial son tends his parents;

sentences.zh: 見有惡於君，若鷹鸇之逐鳥雀」。

translations.literal: when one sees what is harmful to one's lord, one should drive it away as a hawk or kite pursues sparrows."
translations.idiomatic: when you see something that harms your lord, drive it out as a hawk drives sparrows."

sentences.zh: 耿弇不以賊遺君父，前史以為美談。

translations.literal: Geng Yan did not leave bandits to his lord and father; earlier histories regarded this as a fine anecdote.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yan refused to leave rebels alive for his sovereign and father—a story earlier histories praise.

sentences.zh: 而喜軍中五千人，皆親經反逆，攜養左右，豈有奉上之心！

translations.literal: Yet five thousand men in Xi's army all personally experienced rebellion; he keeps and nurtures them at his side—how could they have a heart to serve the throne!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu Xi keeps five thousand men at his side who personally took part in rebellion. How could such men serve the throne!

sentences.zh: 喜意志張大，每稱漢高、魏武，本是何人。

translations.literal: Xi's ambitions swell greatly; he often cites Han Gaozu and Wei Wu—who were they in their origins?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's ambitions have grown swollen. He constantly invokes Han Gaozu and Cao Cao—as if asking who he thinks he is.

sentences.zh: 近忽通啟，求解軍任，乞中散大夫。

translations.literal: Recently he suddenly sent an official communication requesting release from his military command and begging for the title of Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He has just petitioned to be relieved of military command and appointed a Palace Attendant instead.

sentences.zh: 喜是何人，乃敢作此舉止！

translations.literal: Who is Xi, that he dares such behavior!
translations.idiomatic: Who does Wu Xi think he is, to dare such conduct!

sentences.zh: 且當今邊疆未寧，正是喜輸蹄領之日，若以自處之宜，當節儉廉慎，靜掃閉門，不興外物交關；

translations.literal: Moreover, the frontier borders are not yet secure—it is precisely the day for Xi to offer his hooves and lead; if one considers how he ought to comport himself, he should be frugal, honest, and cautious, quietly sweep and close his doors, and have no dealings with outside parties;
translations.idiomatic: The frontier is still unsettled. This is when Wu Xi should be offering every ounce of service. Instead he ought to be living frugally and cautiously, keeping to himself and avoiding outside dealings;

sentences.zh: 專心奉上，何得以其蜼螭，高自比擬。

translations.literal: Devoting himself wholly to serving the throne—how can he with his earthworm-and-lizard nature hold himself up for lofty comparison?
translations.idiomatic: He should devote himself entirely to the throne. Instead this base-born creature dares compare himself to the great.

sentences.zh: 當是自顧愆釁，事宣遐邇，又見壽寂之流徙，施脩林被擊，物惡傷類，內懷憂恐，故興此計，圖欲自安。

translations.literal: It must be that he reflects on his accumulated offenses, known far and near; he also sees Shou Ji's banishment and Shi Xiulin's being struck down—creatures hate to see their kind harmed—and inwardly harbors worry and fear; therefore he devised this plan, seeking to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: No doubt he sees his crimes exposed everywhere, watches men like Shou Ji exiled and Shi Xiulin struck down—bad men tremble when their kind fall—and devised this scheme to save his own skin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷之士及大臣藩鎮，喜殆無所畏者，畏者唯吾一人耳。

translations.literal: Among court officials, great ministers, and frontier governors, there is scarcely anyone Xi fears; the only one he fears is me alone.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials, great ministers, and frontier governors—Wu Xi fears almost none of them. He fears only me.

sentences.zh: 人生脩短，不可豫量，若吾壽百年，世間無喜，何所虧損。

translations.literal: Human life long or short cannot be foreknown; if I live a hundred years and there is no Xi in the realm, what loss would there be?
translations.idiomatic: No one knows how long one will live. If I reign a hundred years and Wu Xi is gone, what would the realm lose?

sentences.zh: 若使吾四月中疾患不得治力，天下豈可有喜一人。

translations.literal: If I should fall ill in the fourth month and lack the strength to govern, how could the realm tolerate Xi alone?
translations.idiomatic: If I sicken this fourth month and lose the strength to rule, how could the empire survive with Wu Xi still in power?

sentences.zh: 尋喜心跡，不可奉守文之主，豈可遭國家間隙，有可乘之會邪！

translations.literal: Consider Xi's heart and tracks—he cannot serve a ruler who upholds written law; how could the state encounter a gap and a seizable opportunity!
translations.idiomatic: Given Wu Xi's dispositions, he would never serve a ruler who governed by law. What if the state were struck by crisis and he saw his chance!

sentences.zh: 世人多云，「時可畏，國政嚴」。

translations.literal: Many in the world say, "The times are to be feared; state governance is severe."
translations.idiomatic: Many people say, "These are fearful times; the government is harsh."

sentences.zh: 歷觀有天下，御億兆，仗威齊眾，何代不然。

translations.literal: Looking through those who held the realm, ruled over myriad masses, and relied on awe to align the multitude—what age was otherwise?
translations.idiomatic: Every ruler who held the empire, governed millions, and kept order through authority did the same.

sentences.zh: 故上古象刑，民淳不犯；

translations.literal: Therefore in high antiquity there was the punishment of symbolic forms, and the people were pure and did not offend;
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity symbolic punishments sufficed because the people were upright and did not transgress;

sentences.zh: 後聖懲偽，易以剠墨。

translations.literal: Later sages punished deception and replaced it with branding and tattooing.
translations.idiomatic: Later sage rulers had to punish deceit with branding and tattoo instead.

sentences.zh: 唐堯至仁，不赦四凶之罪；

translations.literal: Even Tang Yao, most humane, did not pardon the crimes of the Four Evils;
translations.idiomatic: Even the supremely humane Emperor Yao did not spare the Four Evils;

sentences.zh: 漢高大度，而急三傑之誅。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu was magnanimous, yet urgently executed the Three Heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Even magnanimous Han Gaozu moved swiftly to execute the three great generals.

sentences.zh: 且太公為治，先華士之刑；

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Grand Duke governed, he first applied the punishment to Hua Shi;
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Duke Jiang Ziya governed Qi, he first executed the recluses who refused office;

sentences.zh: 宣尼作宰，肆少正之戮。

translations.literal: When Confucius served as minister, he executed Shaozheng Mao.
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius served as minister of Lu, he had Shaozheng Mao put to death.

sentences.zh: 自昔力安社稷，功濟蒼生，班劍引前，笳鼓陪後，不能保此者，歷代無數。

translations.literal: From old, those who with force settled the altars of state and whose merit rescued the people—with ranked swords leading before and reed-drums following behind—unable to preserve this: such men are countless through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, countless men who saved the state, served the people, and marched with honors could not keep their fortune to the end.

sentences.zh: 養之以福，十分有一耳。

translations.literal: Those nourished to fortune: barely one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Of such men, scarcely one in ten kept his blessings to the end.

sentences.zh: 至若喜之深罪，其得免乎？

translations.literal: As for Xi's deep crimes—can he escape?
translations.idiomatic: As for Wu Xi's grave offenses—can he possibly escape punishment?

sentences.zh: 夫富之與貴，雖以功績致之，必由道德守之。

translations.literal: Wealth and eminence, though attained through merit and achievement, must be preserved through virtue and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and rank may be won by merit, but they can be kept only through virtue.

sentences.zh: 故善始者未足稱奇，令終者乃可重耳。

translations.literal: Therefore one who begins well is not enough to be called extraordinary; only one who finishes well is truly to be valued.
translations.idiomatic: A good beginning is nothing remarkable; only a good ending earns true respect.

sentences.zh: 凡置官養士，本在利國，當其為利，愛之如赤子；

translations.literal: Whenever offices are established and scholars nurtured, it is fundamentally to benefit the state; when they benefit, love them as an infant;
translations.idiomatic: The purpose of appointing officials and maintaining a staff is to serve the state. While they serve it well, cherish them as you would an infant;

sentences.zh: 及其為害，畏之若仇讎，豈暇遠尋初功，而應忍受終敝耳。

translations.literal: when they become harmful, fear them as bitter enemies—how could one have leisure to search far for early merit and accordingly endure their final corruption?
translations.idiomatic: when they become harmful, fear them as enemies. One cannot cling to early merit and tolerate their final rot.

sentences.zh: 將之為用，譬如餌藥，當人羸冷，資散石以全身；

translations.literal: Using a general is like applying medicine: when a man is weak and chilled, powdered medicinals are used to preserve the body;
translations.idiomatic: Employing a general is like taking medicine: when a man is weak and chilled, a mild tonic restores his health;

sentences.zh: 及熱勢發動，去堅積以止患。

translations.literal: when the heat syndrome stirs and mounts, remove the strong accumulations to stop the affliction.
translations.idiomatic: when fever flares, strong purgatives must be used to stop the disease.

sentences.zh: 豈憶始時之益，不計後日之損；

translations.literal: How can one recall the benefit at the first and not reckon the damage on later days;
translations.idiomatic: One cannot dwell on the early benefit and ignore the later harm;

sentences.zh: 存前者之賞，抑當今之罰。

translations.literal: preserve the reward of earlier days and suppress the punishment of the present?
translations.idiomatic: nor grant past rewards while withholding present punishment.

sentences.zh: 非忘其功，勢不獲已耳。

translations.literal: It is not forgetting his merit—circumstances leave no alternative.
translations.idiomatic: This is not ingratitude—it is necessity.

sentences.zh: 喜罪釁山積，志意難容，雖有功效，不足自補，交為國患，焉得不除。

translations.literal: Xi's crimes and offenses pile like mountains; his intent is hard to tolerate; though he had achievements, they are insufficient to redeem himself; he has become a calamity to the state—how can he not be removed?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi's offenses tower like a mountain. His ambitions cannot be tolerated. Past service cannot atone for it. He has become a national disaster and must be removed.

sentences.zh: 且欲防微杜漸，憂在未萌，不欲方幅露其罪惡，明當嚴詔切之，令自為其所。

translations.literal: Moreover I wish to check the subtle and stop the gradual, worrying before it sprouts; I do not wish to expose his crimes openly in full measure, but tomorrow will issue stern edicts pressing him, letting him resolve matters himself.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to stop this before it spreads and act before trouble erupts. I will not publish every detail of his crimes, but will issue stern orders tomorrow and leave him to settle his own account.

sentences.zh: 卿諸人將相大臣，股肱所寄，賞罰事重，應與卿等論之，卿意並謂云何？

translations.literal: You generals, ministers, and great officials—the limbs upon whom I rely—reward and punishment are weighty matters and ought to be discussed with you. What do you all think?
translations.idiomatic: You are my arms and legs, my generals and ministers. Reward and punishment are grave matters, and I should consult you. What is your view?

sentences.zh: 及喜死，發詔賻賜。

translations.literal: When Xi died, an edict was issued granting funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi died, the throne issued an edict granting funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 子徽民，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Huimin inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huimin inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi dynasty took the throne, the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 黃回，竟陵郡軍人也。

translations.literal: Huang Hui was a soldier of Jingling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui was a common soldier from Jingling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 出身充郡府雜役，稍至傳教。

translations.literal: He entered service filling miscellaneous duties in the prefectural office, gradually rising to message bearer.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a menial in the prefectural office and gradually worked up to messenger.

sentences.zh: 臧質為郡，轉齋帥，及去職，將回自隨。

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi governed the commandery, Hui became quartermaster; when Zhi left office he took Hui with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi was prefect, Hui became quartermaster. When Zhi left office, he took Hui with him.

sentences.zh: 質為雍州，回復為齋帥。

translations.literal: When Zhi governed Yong Province, Hui again served as quartermaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi took Yong Province, Hui again served as his quartermaster.

sentences.zh: 質討元兇，回隨從有功，免軍戶。

translations.literal: When Zhi attacked the prime rebel, Hui followed and had merit, and was freed from military-household status.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi campaigned against Liu Shao, Hui followed and distinguished himself, winning release from military-household status.

sentences.zh: 質在江州，擢領白直隊主。

translations.literal: When Zhi was at Jiang Province, Hui was promoted to lead the white-guard squad captain.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhi held Jiang Province, Hui was promoted to captain of the white-guard squad.

sentences.zh: 隨質於梁山敗走向豫章，為臺軍主謝承祖所錄，付江州作部，遇赦得原。

translations.literal: Following Zhi in defeat at Liang Mountain and fleeing toward Yuzhang, he was arrested by Palace Army Commander Xie Chengzu, handed over to Jiang Province for labor service, and pardoned through amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhi's defeat at Mount Liang and flight toward Yuzhang, Hui was arrested by Palace Army Commander Xie Chengzu, assigned to labor in Jiang Province, and later pardoned.

sentences.zh: 回因下都，於宣陽門與人相打，詐稱江夏王義恭馬客，鞭二百，付右尚方。

translations.literal: Hui then went down to the capital; at Xuanyang Gate he got into a fight with someone, falsely claiming to be a groom of Prince Jiangxia Liu Yigong; he received two hundred lashes and was handed over to the Right Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Hui later went to the capital. At Xuanyang Gate he brawled with someone and falsely claimed to be a groom of Prince Jiangxia. He was flogged two hundred times and sent to the Right Workshops.

sentences.zh: 會中書舍人戴明寶被繫，差回為戶伯，性便辟勤緊，奉事明寶，竭盡心力。

translations.literal: It happened that Palace Secretary Dai Mingbao was imprisoned; Hui was assigned as house steward. By nature agile and industrious, he served Mingbao, exhausting all his heart and strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Secretary Dai Mingbao was imprisoned, Hui was assigned as his house steward. Quick and diligent by nature, he served Mingbao with complete devotion.

sentences.zh: 明寶尋得原赦，委任如初，啟免回，以領隨身隊，統知宅及江西墅事。

translations.literal: Mingbao soon received pardon and was entrusted as before; he petitioned to release Hui and had him lead the personal guard squad, overseeing the residence and the villa west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Mingbao was soon pardoned and restored to favor. He petitioned for Hui's release and made him head of his personal guard, putting him in charge of the house and the villa west of the river.

sentences.zh: 性有功藝，觸類多能，明寶甚寵任之。

translations.literal: By nature skilled in martial arts, capable in many categories, Mingbao greatly favored and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had a gift for arms and many other skills. Mingbao favored and relied on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽初，桂陽王休範為逆，回以屯騎校尉領軍隸齊王，於新亭創詐降之計，事在休範傳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui in the reign of the Later Deposed Emperor, Prince of Guiyang Liu Xiufan rebelled; Hui, as Commandant of Cavalry for Encampments commanding troops under the Prince of Qi, devised the feigned-surrender plan at Xinting—the account is in Xiufan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor, Prince of Guiyang Liu Xiufan rebelled. Hui, as Commandant of Encampment Cavalry under the Prince of Qi, devised the false-surrender stratagem at Xinting—the full account is in Xiufan's biography.

sentences.zh: 回見休範可乘，謂張敬兒曰：「卿可取之，我誓不殺諸王。」

translations.literal: Hui saw that Xiufan could be exploited and said to Zhang Jinger: "You can take him—I swear I will not kill any prince."
translations.idiomatic: Hui saw that Xiufan was vulnerable and told Zhang Jinger, "You take him. I swear I will not kill any prince."

sentences.zh: 敬兒即日斬休範。

translations.literal: That same day Jinger beheaded Xiufan.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Zhang Jinger beheaded Xiufan.

sentences.zh: 事平，轉回驍騎將軍，加輔師將軍，進爵為侯，改封聞喜縣，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Hui was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry, given the additional title of General Assisting the Army, advanced in rank to marquis, given Wenxi County with an added fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, Hui was made General of Valiant Cavalry and General Assisting the Army, raised to marquis, and enfeoffed in Wenxi County with one thousand additional households.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷冠軍將軍、南琅邪、濟陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to General Who Conquers Barbarians and Prefect of the two commanderies of Nan Langye and Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and made prefect of Nan Langye and Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素反，回又率軍前討，假節。

translations.literal: Prince of Jianping Liu Jingsu rebelled; Hui again led troops forward to suppress him, with provisional credentials.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jianping Liu Jingsu rebelled, Hui again marched against him with provisional credentials.

sentences.zh: 城平之日，回軍先入，又以景素讓張倪奴，回增邑五百戶，進號征虜將軍，加散騎常侍，太守如故。

translations.literal: On the day the city fell, Hui's army entered first; he also yielded Jingsu to Zhang Ninu; Hui received five hundred additional households, was promoted to General Who Conquers the Barbarians, given the additional title of Regular Palace Attendant, and retained his prefecture as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Hui's troops entered first. He handed Jingsu over to Zhang Ninu. Hui received five hundred more households, was promoted to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Regular Palace Attendant, and kept his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷右衛將軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to General of the Right Guard, retaining his palace attendant title as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to General of the Right Guard, retaining his title as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之反，以回為使持節、督郢州、司州之義陽諸軍事、平西將軍、郢州刺史，給鼓吹一部，率眾出新亭為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Hui was made bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander of Ying Province and military affairs of Yiyang in Si Province, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Ying Province, granted one set of drums and horns, and led troops out from Xinting as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Hui was appointed Area Commander of Ying and Yiyang, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Ying Province, with drums and horns, and marched from Xinting as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 未發，而袁粲據石頭為亂，回與新亭諸將帥任候伯、彭文之、王宜興、孫曇瓘等謀應粲。

translations.literal: Before departing, Yuan Can seized Shitou in rebellion; Hui with the commanders at Xinting—Ren Houbo, Peng Wenzhi, Wang Yixing, and Sun Tanqian—plotted to respond to Can.
translations.idiomatic: Before they marched, Yuan Can seized Shitou in rebellion. Hui and the Xinting commanders Ren Houbo, Peng Wenzhi, Wang Yixing, and Sun Tanqian plotted to join him.

sentences.zh: 粲事發，候伯等並乘船赴石頭，唯曇瓘先至得入，候伯等至，而粲已平。

translations.literal: When Can's plot broke, Houbo and the others all took boats to Shitou; only Tanqian arrived first and got in; when Houbo and the others arrived, Can had already been suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, Houbo and the others sailed for Shitou. Only Tanqian got inside first. By the time the rest arrived, Can had already been defeated.

sentences.zh: 回本期詰旦率所領從御道直向臺門，攻齊王於朝堂，事既不果，齊王撫之如舊。

translations.literal: Hui had planned at dawn the next day to lead his command straight along the Imperial Way to the palace gate and attack the Prince of Qi in the court hall; when the affair failed, the Prince of Qi treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had planned to lead his men at dawn along the Imperial Way straight to the palace gate and attack the Prince of Qi in the court hall. When the plot failed, the Prince of Qi treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 回與宜興素不協，慮或反告，因其不從處分，斬之。

translations.literal: Hui and Yixing had long been incompatible; fearing he might inform against him in turn, he executed him on the pretext that he had disobeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Wang Yixing had never got along. Fearing Yixing might turn informer, he had him executed for disobeying orders.

sentences.zh: 宜興，吳興人也。

translations.literal: Yixing was a man of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yixing was a native of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 形狀短小，而果勁有膽力。

translations.literal: Short in stature, yet resolute, vigorous, and bold.
translations.idiomatic: He was short in build, but resolute, fierce, and fearless.

sentences.zh: 少年時為劫，不須伴，郡討逐圍繞數十重，終莫能擒。

translations.literal: In youth he became a bandit and needed no accomplices; when the commandery pursued him, encirclement after encirclement—scores of them—could never capture him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he turned bandit and needed no partners. Commandery troops hunted him through dozens of encircling lines and never took him.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始中，為將，在壽陽間擊索虜，每以少制多，挺身深入，無所畏憚，虜眾值宜興，皆引避不敢當。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era under Emperor Ming, he served as a general; between Shouyang he struck the Northern Wei enemies, repeatedly using few to overcome many, plunging deep without fear. Whenever the enemy forces met Yixing, they all drew back and dared not oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era of Emperor Ming he served as a general. Fighting around Shouyang against the Northern Wei, he again and again beat larger forces with smaller ones, charging deep without hesitation. Enemy troops who ran into Yixing always fell back rather than face him.

sentences.zh: 稍至寧朔將軍，羽林監。

translations.literal: He gradually rose to General Who Pacifies the North and Director of the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In time he rose to General Who Pacifies the North and Director of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 以平建平王景素功，封長壽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in suppressing Prince Jingsu of Jianping, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changshou with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For helping put down Prince Jingsu of Jianping, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changshou with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 至是，為屯騎校尉，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: At this time he was Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry with the additional title General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry, with the additional rank of General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 回進軍未至郢州，而沈攸之敗走。

translations.literal: Hui advanced but had not yet reached Ying Province when Shen Youzhi was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was still marching and had not yet reached Ying Province when Shen Youzhi was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 回至鎮，進號鎮西將軍，改督為都督。

translations.literal: Hui returned to his post and was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West; his supervisory rank was changed to area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui returned to his command, he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West, and his supervisory title was upgraded to area commander.

sentences.zh: 回不樂停郢州，固求南兗，遂率部曲輒還。

translations.literal: Hui did not wish to remain at Ying Province and pressed hard for Southern Yanzhou; he then led his personal troops straight back.
translations.idiomatic: Hui did not want to stay at Ying Province and pressed insistently for Southern Yanzhou, then marched his personal troops straight home.

sentences.zh: 改封安陸郡公，增邑二千戶，并前三千七百戶。

translations.literal: He was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Anlu Commandery, with two thousand additional households—three thousand seven hundred in all with his previous fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Anlu Commandery, with two thousand more households added to his fief—for three thousand seven hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 改都督南兗、徐、兗、青、冀五州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、南兗州刺史，加散騎常侍，持節如故。

translations.literal: He was made Area Commander of military affairs in the five provinces of Southern Yanzhou, Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, retaining his staff of authority as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made area commander of military affairs in Southern Yanzhou, Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, with the added title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, keeping his staff of authority as before.

sentences.zh: 齊王以回終為禍亂，乃上表曰：「黃回出自廝伍，本無信行，仰值泰始，謬被驅馳，階藉風雲，累叨顯伍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, believing Hui would ultimately bring calamity and rebellion, submitted a memorial: "Huang Hui rose from the ranks of menials; he originally had no trustworthy conduct. By good fortune of the Taishi era he was absurdly pressed into service; riding the winds of fortune he repeatedly attained distinguished stations.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, convinced that Hui would end in rebellion and ruin, submitted a memorial: "Huang Hui came up from the ranks. He never had a trustworthy character. In the Taishi era he was absurdly swept into service; carried upward by changing fortune, he climbed again and again into high office.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之作逆，事切戎機，臣闇於知人，冀其搏噬，遣統前鋒，竟不接刃。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, the matter was urgent for military affairs. I was dull in judging men and hoped he would fight fiercely; I sent him to command the vanguard, yet he never crossed blades.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, the crisis was immediate. I misjudged the man and hoped he would tear into the enemy. I sent him to lead the vanguard, and he never once crossed swords.

sentences.zh: 軍至郢城，乘威迫脅，陵掠所加，必先尊貴。

translations.literal: When the army reached Ying city, riding on its momentum he coerced and oppressed; whenever he looted, he always struck the eminent first.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Ying city, he used its momentum to bully and extort. Whatever he plundered, he took first from the highest ranks.

sentences.zh: 武陵王馬器服咸被虜奪，城內文武，剝剔靡遺。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wuling's horses, fittings, and garments were all seized; within the city the civil and military officials were stripped to the last item.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wuling's horses, trappings, and robes were all seized. Inside the city, civil and military officials were stripped of everything.

sentences.zh: 及至還都，縱恣彌甚，先朝御服，猶有二輿，弓劍遺思，尚在車府。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital his wantonness grew even worse. Of the imperial regalia from the former reign, two carriages still remained; bow and sword left in remembrance were still kept in the chariot office.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, his arrogance only grew. Of the former emperor's regalia, two imperial carriages still remained; memorial bow and sword were still kept in the chariot office.

sentences.zh: 回遂啟求，以擬私用，僭侮無厭，罔顧天極。

translations.literal: Hui then petitioned to demand them for private use—presumptuous and insolent without end, heedless of the pinnacle of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then petitioned to take them for his private use—insolent beyond measure, with no regard for the throne.

sentences.zh: 又廣納逋亡，多受劫盜，親信此等，並為爪牙。

translations.literal: Moreover he broadly took in fugitives and received many bandits and robbers; he trusted such men all as his claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: He also took in fugitives on a wide scale and welcomed bandits and robbers, making such men his trusted enforcers.

sentences.zh: 觀其凶狡，憂在不測，惡積罪著，非可含忍，應加剷除，以明國憲。

translations.literal: Seeing his fierce cunning, I fear what cannot be foreseen; his wickedness has piled up and his crimes are manifest—they cannot be tolerated. He should be cut down to clarify the laws of the state.
translations.idiomatic: His savage cunning makes the future impossible to read. His crimes have piled up until they can no longer be borne. He should be removed to make the law clear.

sentences.zh: 尋其釁狀，實宜極法，但嘗經將帥，微有塵露，罪疑從輕，事炳前策，請在降減，特原餘嗣。

translations.literal: Examining the evidence of his offenses, the full penalty is truly warranted; but having once held command, he has slight merit in the field. Where guilt is doubtful, apply the lighter punishment—as precedent makes plain, I ask that the sentence be reduced and his descendants specially spared.
translations.idiomatic: By the full measure of his guilt he deserves the extreme penalty; yet he once held command and has a little merit on campaign. Where the law allows doubt to weigh in the lighter direction, as precedent requires, I ask that his sentence be reduced and his descendants spared.

sentences.zh: 臣過荷隆寄，言必罄誠，謹陳管穴，式遵弘典，伏願聖明，特垂允鑒。

translations.literal: Your subject has received excessive favor and trust; my words must be exhaustive in sincerity. I respectfully offer this humble glimpse and follow the great precedents, bowing in hope that sagely clarity will specially grant approval and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has been entrusted beyond his deserts, and I speak now with all the sincerity I have. I offer this narrow view in reverence for the great precedents, and beg Your Sagely Majesty to grant your approval.

sentences.zh: 臣思不出位，誠昧甄才，追言既往，伏增慚恧。」

translations.literal: Your subject's thoughts do not overstep his station; I am truly blind in discerning talent. Speaking now of what has passed, I am deeply ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: My thoughts do not overstep my office, yet I confess I failed to judge men rightly. To speak now of what is already past fills me with shame."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「黃回擢自凡豎，夙負疵釁，貰以憲綱，收基搏噬。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Huang Hui was plucked from common soldiery; long he bore stains and offenses. Pardoned under the laws, he took base reward and fought like a beast of prey.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Huang Hui was pulled up from the common ranks. He had long carried stains upon him. Spared by the law, he fed on opportunity and fought like a predator.

sentences.zh: 雖勤效累著，而屢懷干紀。

translations.literal: Though his diligent achievements accumulated and stood out, repeatedly he harbored designs against the discipline of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Though his service mounted and his deeds stood out, again and again he nursed designs against the order of the state.

sentences.zh: 新亭背叛，投拜寇場，異規既扇，廟律幾殆，幸得張敬兒提戈直奮，元惡受戮。

translations.literal: At Xinting he betrayed us and bowed to the enemy's camp; once his divergent schemes were fanned, the laws of the ancestral temple were nearly destroyed. Fortunately Zhang Jinger seized his halberd and charged straight forward—the arch villain received execution.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinting he turned traitor and bowed to the rebels. Once his separate plot was set in motion, the laws of the ancestral temple nearly collapsed. Only because Zhang Jinger seized his halberd and struck straight at the enemy was the chief villain brought to execution.

sentences.zh: 及景素結逆，履霜歲久，乃密通音譯，潛送器杖，氛沴克霽，狡謀方顯。

translations.literal: When Jingsu formed treason, frost had lain long upon the ground; yet Hui secretly exchanged messages and covertly sent weapons. Only when the miasma cleared did his cunning plot come to light.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsu plotted rebellion, the warning signs had been there for years. Hui secretly exchanged messages with him and smuggled him arms. Only when the evil air cleared did his treacherous design show itself.

sentences.zh: 每存容掩，冀能悛革，故裂茅升爵，均榮勳寵。

translations.literal: Each time we preserved forbearance and cover, hoping he might repent and reform; thus split-clay enfeoffments and raised ranks, sharing honor and merit with the rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Time after time we covered for him, hoping he would turn back. That is why he was given fiefs and raised in rank, sharing honors with men of real merit.

sentences.zh: 凶詖有本，險慝滋深，構誘敬兒，志相攻陷，悖圖未遂，佷戾彌甚。

translations.literal: His vicious perversity had deep roots; treacherous wickedness grew ever deeper. He framed and enticed Jinger, intending mutual ruin; though his rebellious design did not succeed, his brutish defiance grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: His evil had deep roots, and his treachery only deepened. He plotted against Jinger and tried to drag him down with him. Though the rebellion failed, his brutish defiance grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 近軍次郢鎮，劫逼府主，兼挾私計，多所徵索，主局咨疑，便加捶楚，專肆暴慢，罔顧彝則。

translations.literal: Recently his army halted at Ying garrison; he robbed and coerced the prefect, and together with private designs made many demands. When the chief clerks raised questions, he at once applied beatings—wantonly violent and arrogant, heedless of ritual norms.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when his army halted at Ying, he robbed and intimidated the prefect and, pursuing private ends, made endless demands. When the chief clerks questioned him, he had them beaten on the spot—violent, arrogant, and contemptuous of all rule.

sentences.zh: 膺牧西蕃，徽賁惟厚，曾不知感，猶懷忿怨。

translations.literal: Entrusted to govern the western frontier, his badges and rewards were thick indeed; he never knew gratitude and still nursed grievance and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusted with the western frontier, he was heaped with honors and rewards. He felt no gratitude and still brooded on grievance.

sentences.zh: 李安民述任河、濟，星管未周，貪據襟要，苦祈回奪。

translations.literal: Li Anmin was narrating his assignment on the Yellow and Ji rivers; his term in office had not yet run its course, yet Hui greedily seized key positions and pestered to wrest them back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anmin was still carrying out his assignment on the Yellow and Ji rivers; his term had not yet ended. Hui greedily seized key posts and pestered the court to take them from him.

sentences.zh: 黷謁弗已，叨侈無度，遂請求御輿，僭擬私飾。

translations.literal: His impertinent petitions did not cease; his presumptuous extravagance knew no limit—he went so far as to request the imperial carriage and model private adornment on it.
translations.idiomatic: His brazen petitions never stopped. His presumptuous excess knew no bounds. He even asked for the imperial carriage and fitted out his own in imitation of it.

sentences.zh: 又招萃賊黨，初不啟聞，傷風蠹化，莫此之甚。

translations.literal: Moreover he gathered bandit parties without ever reporting it—nothing more corrosive to custom and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered bands of outlaws without reporting it—nothing could do more harm to public morals.

sentences.zh: 宜明繩裁，肅正刑書，便收付廷尉，依法窮治。」

translations.literal: The law's measure should be made clear; punishments should be solemnly rectified. Let him be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice for exhaustive prosecution according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The law must be made clear and punishment restored to its proper severity. Let him be arrested and handed to the Minister of Justice for full prosecution under the law."

sentences.zh: 回死時，年五十二。

translations.literal: When Hui died he was fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was fifty-two when he died.

sentences.zh: 子僧念，尚書左民郎，竟陵相，未發，從誅。

translations.literal: His son Sengnian was Left Clerk of the People's Section in the Ministry of Works and had been appointed Administrator of Jingling, but before departing he was executed along with his father.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengnian was Left Clerk of the People's Section in the Ministry of Works and had been appointed administrator of Jingling, but before he could take up the post he was executed with his father.

sentences.zh: 回既貴，祗事戴明寶甚謹，言必自名。

translations.literal: Once Hui had risen high, he served Dai Mingbao with great reverence; whenever he spoke he always gave his own name.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui rose to power, he served Dai Mingbao with scrupulous devotion, always naming himself when he spoke.

sentences.zh: 每至明寶許，屏人獨進，未嘗敢坐。

translations.literal: Whenever he came to Mingbao's quarters he dismissed attendants and entered alone; he never dared to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he visited Mingbao he sent away attendants and entered alone, and never dared to sit down.

sentences.zh: 躬至帳下及入內，料檢有無，隨乏供送，以此為常。

translations.literal: In person he went to the tent entrance and inside, checking what was lacking and supplying whatever was needed—a practice he maintained as routine.
translations.idiomatic: He went in person to Mingbao's tent and inner rooms, checking what was missing and sending whatever was needed. This became his daily habit.

sentences.zh: 先是，王蘊為湘州，潁川庾佩玉為蘊寧朔府長史、長沙內史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Yun served as Inspector of Xiang Province; Yingchuan's Yu Peiyu was chief secretary of Yun's Pacifying the North headquarters and Administrator of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Yun was inspector of Xiang Province, Yu Peiyu of Yingchuan served as chief secretary of Yun's Pacifying-the-North headquarters and as administrator of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 蘊去職，南中郎將、湘州刺史南陽王翽未之任，權以佩玉行府州事。

translations.literal: When Yun left office, General of the Southern Palace Gentlemen and Inspector of Xiang Prince Hui of Nanyang had not yet taken up his post; Yu Peiyu was temporarily entrusted with the duties of the headquarters and province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun left office, Prince Hui of Nanyang had been appointed general of the southern palace gentlemen and inspector of Xiang but had not yet arrived. Yu Peiyu was temporarily put in charge of headquarters and provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 先遣中兵參軍、臨湘令韓幼宗領軍戍防湘州，與佩玉共事，不美。

translations.literal: Previously the Central Army Staff Officer and Prefect of Linxiang Han Youzong had been sent to lead troops garrisoning Xiang Province; he and Peiyu worked together but relations were poor.
translations.idiomatic: Han Youzong, central army staff officer and prefect of Linxiang, had already been sent to garrison Xiang Province with troops. He and Peiyu served together, but the arrangement went badly.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之為逆，佩玉、幼宗各不相信，幼宗密圖，佩玉知其謀，襲殺幼宗。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Peiyu and Youzong each distrusted the other; Youzong plotted in secret, and Peiyu, learning of his design, attacked and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Peiyu and Youzong lost trust in each other. Youzong plotted in secret; Peiyu learned of it and struck first, killing him.

sentences.zh: 回至郢州，遣輔國將軍任候伯行湘州事，候伯以佩玉兩端，輒殺之。

translations.literal: When Hui reached Ying Province he sent General Who Assists the State Ren Houbo to administer Xiang Province affairs; Houbo, deeming Peiyu double-dealing, immediately had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached Ying Province he sent Ren Houbo, General Who Assists the State, to handle Xiang affairs. Houbo judged Peiyu two-faced and had him killed at once.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史呂安國之鎮，齊王使安國誅候伯。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Xiang Lü Anguo reached his post, the Prince of Qi had Anguo execute Houbo.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Anguo arrived to take up the inspectorate of Xiang, the Prince of Qi ordered him to execute Houbo.

sentences.zh: 彭文之，泰山人也。

translations.literal: Peng Wenzhi was a man of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Wenzhi was a native of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 以軍功稍至龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Through military merit he gradually rose to General Who Supervises the Dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Through battlefield merit he rose in time to General Who Supervises the Dragons.

sentences.zh: 討建平王景素功，封葛陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in suppressing Prince Jingsu of Jianping, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Geyang with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For helping suppress Prince Jingsu of Jianping, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Geyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 順帝初，為輔國將軍、左軍將軍、南濮陽太守、直閣，領右細杖蕩主。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Shun's reign he was General Who Assists the State, General of the Left Army, Prefect of Southern Puyang, Attendant at the Inner Gate, and chief of the right fine-staff guard detail.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Shun's reign he was General Who Assists the State, General of the Left Army, prefect of Southern Puyang, attendant at the inner gate, and chief of the right fine-staff guard.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之平後，齊王收之下獄，賜死。

translations.literal: After Shen Youzhi was suppressed, the Prince of Qi had him arrested and imprisoned, and granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen Youzhi was defeated, the Prince of Qi had him arrested, thrown into prison, and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 孫曇瓘，吳郡富陽人也。

translations.literal: Sun Tanqian was a man of Fuyang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tanqian was a native of Fuyang in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 驍果有氣力，以軍功稍進，至是為寧朔將軍、越州刺史。

translations.literal: Bold and capable, strong of body, he advanced gradually through military merit; at this time he was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yue Province.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce, able, and physically powerful, he climbed by military merit. By then he was General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yue Province.

sentences.zh: 於石頭叛走，逃竄經時，後於秣陵縣禽獲，伏誅。

translations.literal: At Shitou he rebelled and fled; after wandering in hiding for some time, he was later captured in Moling County and executed.
translations.idiomatic: At Shitou he rebelled and fled. After long months on the run he was captured in Moling County and executed.

sentences.zh: 回同時為將者，臨淮任農夫，沛郡周寧民，南郡高道慶，並以武用顧。

translations.literal: Generals who served at the same time as Hui included Ren Nongfu of Linhuai, Zhou Ningmin of Pei Commandery, and Gao Daoqing of Nan Commandery—all remembered for martial service.
translations.idiomatic: Among the generals who rose alongside Hui were Ren Nongfu of Linhuai, Zhou Ningmin of Pei Commandery, and Gao Daoqing of Nan Commandery—all men valued for their fighting.

sentences.zh: 農夫稍至強弩將軍。

translations.literal: Nongfu rose in time to General of the Strong Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Nongfu rose in time to General of the Strong Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，以東討功，封廣晉縣子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Ming's reign, for merit in the eastern campaign, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Guangjin with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign, for merit on the eastern campaign, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Guangjin with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 東土平定，仍又南討，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When the east was pacified he again joined the southern campaign; his fief was increased by two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the east was pacified he fought again in the south, and his fief was increased by two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 歷射聲校尉，左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He served successively as Colonel Who Shoots at Sound and General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Colonel Who Shoots at Sound and General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 時桂陽王休範在江州，有異志，朝廷慮其下，以農夫為輔師將軍、淮南太守，戍姑孰以防之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Xiufan of Guiyang was in Jiang Province with rebellious intent; the court feared his subordinates, and made Nongfu General Assisting the Army and Prefect of Huainan, garrisoning Guni to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Xiufan of Guiyang held Jiang Province with rebellious intent. The court feared trouble from his followers and made Nongfu General Assisting the Army and prefect of Huainan, stationing him at Guni to block him.

sentences.zh: 休範尋率眾向京邑，奄至近道，農夫棄戍還都。

translations.literal: Xiufan soon led his forces toward the capital; he suddenly arrived on the near road, and Nongfu abandoned his garrison and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan soon marched on the capital and suddenly appeared on the nearest road. Nongfu abandoned his post and fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 休範平，以戰功改封孱陵縣侯，增邑千戶，并前千七百戶。

translations.literal: After Xiufan was suppressed, for battle merit Nongfu was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Canling with one thousand additional households—one thousand seven hundred in all with his previous fief.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiufan was defeated, Nongfu was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Canling for his battle merit, with one thousand more households added—for one thousand seven hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 出為輔師將軍、豫州刺史，尋進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as General Assisting the Army and Inspector of Yu Province; soon he was promoted to General Who Conquers the Enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General Assisting the Army and inspector of Yu Province, and was soon promoted to General Who Conquers the Enemy.

sentences.zh: 明年，入為驍騎將軍，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The next year he entered the capital as General of Valiant Cavalry, with the additional title of Direct and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to court as General of Valiant Cavalry, with the added title of Direct and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 前世加官，唯散騎常侍，無通直員外之文。

translations.literal: In former dynasties the added office was only Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry—there was no mention of Direct Attendant or Acting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier ages the added honor was only Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry. There was no wording for direct attendant or acting attendant.

sentences.zh: 太宗以來，多因軍功至大位，資輕加常侍者，往往通直員外焉。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Ming's reign, many rose to high rank through military merit; those lightly qualified who received the additional title of palace attendant were often given Direct Attendant or Acting Attendant instead.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Ming's time, many men of military merit had risen to high office. Those whose standing was thin but who received the added rank of palace attendant were often given direct or acting attendant titles instead.

sentences.zh: 五年，加征虜將軍，改通直為散騎常侍，驍騎如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given the additional title General Who Conquers the Barbarians; his Direct Attendant title was changed to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, his cavalry generalship remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he received the added title General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and his direct-attendant rank was changed to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry while he kept his cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，追贈左將軍，常侍如故，諡曰貞肅。

translations.literal: That same year he died; posthumously he was given General of the Left Army, his attendant title as before, with the posthumous name Zhensu.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year. Posthumously he was made General of the Left Army, retaining his attendant title, with the posthumous name Upright and Stern.

sentences.zh: 候伯，即農夫弟也。

translations.literal: Houbo was Nongfu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Houbo was Nongfu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 周寧民於鄉里起義討薛安都，亦以軍功至軍校。

translations.literal: Zhou Ningmin raised a righteous force in his home district to suppress Xue Andu, and through military merit rose to an army commandery colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In his home district Zhou Ningmin raised a loyal force to fight Xue Andu and, through military merit, rose to army colonel.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，封贛縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gan County with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taishi era he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gan County with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 官至寧朔將軍、徐州刺史，鍾離太守。

translations.literal: He reached the office of General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Xu Province, and Prefect of Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Pacifies the North, inspector of Xu Province, and prefect of Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 高道慶亦至軍校驍游，以平桂陽王休範功，封樂安縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Gao Daoqing also rose to army colonel of the valiant rangers; for suppressing Prince Xiufan of Guiyang he was enfeoffed as Baron of Le'an with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Daoqing also rose to colonel of the valiant rangers. For suppressing Prince Xiufan of Guiyang he was enfeoffed as Baron of Le'an with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素反，道慶領軍北討，而與景素通謀。

translations.literal: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping rebelled, Daoqing led troops north to suppress him—but secretly communicated with Jingsu in conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping rebelled, Daoqing marched north against him while secretly plotting with Jingsu.

sentences.zh: 及事平，自啟求增邑五百戶，詔加二百，並前五百戶。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he himself petitioned for five hundred additional households; an edict granted two hundred—for five hundred in all with his previous fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was put down he petitioned for five hundred more households. An edict granted two hundred, bringing his fief to five hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 道慶兇險暴橫，求欲無已，有失其意，輒加捶拉，往往有死者，朝廷畏之如虎狼。

translations.literal: Daoqing was vicious, treacherous, and brutally overbearing; his desires never ceased. Anyone who displeased him was promptly beaten and tortured—often unto death. The court feared him as one fears tigers and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing was savage, treacherous, and violently overbearing. His appetites were endless. Anyone who crossed him was beaten and tortured, often to death. The court feared him as it would tigers and wolves.

sentences.zh: 齊王與袁粲等議，收付廷尉，賜死。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi deliberated with Yuan Can and others, had him arrested and delivered to the Minister of Justice, and granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi consulted with Yuan Can and the others, had Daoqing arrested and handed to the Minister of Justice, and ordered him to die.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫豎人匹夫，濟其身業，非世亂莫由也。

translations.literal: The historian comments: Men of low birth and common fellows—to achieve their careers, without an age of chaos they have no path.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: For men of low birth and common stock to make their way in the world, nothing but an age of chaos could have opened the path.

sentences.zh: 以亂世之情，用於治日，其得不亡，亦為幸矣！

translations.literal: To apply the sentiments of a chaotic age to days of good government—that they did not perish is itself good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: To carry the habits of chaos into times of order and still escape destruction was already luck enough!
